articles.title_orig: Rubio oversaw classified memo alleging Nvidia CEO’s ties to suspected Chinese intelligence operative: Report
articles.title_zh: Rubio oversaw classified memo alleging Nvidia CEO’s ties to suspected Chinese intelligence operative: Report
articles.content_orig:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the drafting of a classified intelligence memo warning senior Trump administration officials that Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang had developed a close relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative, the New York Times reported Sunday.
The warning, drafted under Rubio's supervision in the spring of this year, circulated among national security officials holding high-level clearances ahead of a bilateral state visit to China in May by US President Donald Trump.
The document stemmed from electronic surveillance targeting Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who is unrelated to the Nvidia chief. She worked as a senior executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data center company that purchased advanced artificial intelligence processors while under federal investigation for illicitly smuggling semiconductors into mainland China.
When intelligence officials requested the unmasking of an American citizen seen in intercepted communications showing an intimate relationship with her, the review identified the executive as Jensen Huang. Counterintelligence agencies concluded that China's Ministry of State Security had recruited Alice Huang as an operative.
Jensen Huang was initially excluded from the official business delegation traveling with Trump to China. However, after noticing media reports highlighting the absence, Trump intervened directly, arranging for Huang to rendezvous with Air Force One during a refueling stop in Alaska and praising him as "the Great Jensen Huang."
Trump declined to impose restrictions on Huang or the chipmaker, viewing Nvidia's market dominance as vital to US economic competition and financial markets.
Nvidia’s board of directors announced an independent investigation following the reports.
Nvidia earlier said that Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were "not unusual or unexpected," characterizing them as standard commercial engagements and noting that Megaspeed never received classified corporate data or trade secrets.
China in October rejected a related report by the New York Times, dismissing the allegations as "unsubstantiated" and "nothing but a smear against China."
The White House, the State Department and the Central Intelligence Agency declined to comment, the New York Times said, while Alice Huang did not respond to requests for comment.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations he was target of Chinese intelligence effort
articles.title_zh: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations he was target of Chinese intelligence effort
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia has launched an independent investigation of its co-founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, over allegations that he was the target of an intelligence effort by China.
"The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," Nvidia's board of directors said in a statement Sunday. "A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."
The board said it had no reason to believe that the company's secrets or national security were compromised.
"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," the statement said.
A company spokesperson said Huang "fully supports the review" and is committed to continuing to lead the company.
The New York Times reported last month that U.S. authorities were investigating Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, a former executive of the Singapore-based Megaspeed, which buys AI chips from Nvidia. The report claims Jensen Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence officials believe was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security.
Last month, China rejected allegations of a Chinese espionage operation targeting Jensen Huang, describing the claims as "groundless speculation," CBS News partner BBC News reported.
Separately, Jensen Huang admitted to being "unfaithful" to his wife and apologized for hurting her and their children.
"There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," he said in a statement.
Jensen Huang said he had fallen short of his responsibilities to the company's employees, board and shareholders. He said he is "fully committed to NVIDIA" and will work to earn back their trust.
"Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation," he said in a statement. "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully."
"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American," he added.
Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years, according to the Times.
The Associated  Press contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
articles.title_zh: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
articles.content_orig:
Children were among the injured people seen being carried into a nearby hospital
Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say at least 33 people, including women and children, have been killed in air strikes by Saudi Arabia.
There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.
Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.
The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins.
The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital.
Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Saturday. It added that 39 people had been injured.
The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.
The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war.
A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plane landing there.
The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.
Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen.
On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people.
The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.
The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities.
Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh.
The Saudi Ministry of Energy later said the Aramco tower had been hit by falling shrapnel in what it said was an attempted attack.
The state-owned oil company's building suffered minor damage.
A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman whom U.S. intelligence reportedly suspects is a Chinese spy.
Huang, who heads a leading AI chipmaker and is an ally of President Donald Trump , apologized in a message to the company, saying, “I was unfaithful to my wife,” according to The New York Times .
“My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Nvidia announced in a press release Sunday that its board was opening an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
Late last month, the Times reported that Huang had formed a close relationship with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based data center.
Alice Huang is considered by U.S. officials to be a Chinese spy, feeding information to Beijing, according to the report, which cited sources briefed on the surveillance of Alice Huang and other officials and industry experts.
“The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” Sunday’s company press release read.
“While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information.”
CEO Huang supports the investigation and has agreed to cooperate with it, the board said.
There was no word of Huang’s position being in jeopardy, with the board saying it “has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.”
Nvidia is one of the hottest companies in the stock market right now, given the popularity of its chips. It has a market capitalization of roughly 4.5 trillion and was trading at nearly $240 per share early last month.
Huang, like other tech leaders, has flocked to Trump as the president embraces AI. The Nvidia leader and his wife, Lori Huang, attended a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House in September. His attendance wasn’t unusual, given that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg were also there.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia launches investigation after Jensen Huang admits affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.title_zh: Nvidia launches investigation after Jensen Huang admits affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.content_orig:
AI giant Nvidia said Sunday it had opened an investigation into reports its CEO, Jensen Huang, had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
In a statement shared to its website, the tech company said the independent investigation would look into the claims, after Huang wrote to staff in a note later shared with Newsweek that he had an affair. The New York Times reported the woman in question, a business executive, had been found to be a Chinese spy by United States officials.
The Times said Friday that a memo was shard among Trump administration officials last spring, showing the businesswoman had been working as a spy for China 's Ministry of State Security.
"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," Nvidia said in its statement. "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information."
A spokesperson for Nvidia told Newsweek that the news would not slow the company down.
"Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption," the spokesperson said.
Newsweek reached out to the U.S. State Department for comment Sunday afternoon.
Huang is a close ally of President Donald Trump and a leading figure in the world of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
The 63-year-old was born in Taiwan and spent his childhood in Thailand, before moving to the U.S. He co-founded Nvidia in 1993, alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, and he has been the company's CEO since its founding.
Nvidia made its name producing graphics hardware for gaming, but it eventually transformed into one of the leading tech companies focused on AI, as well as autonomous vehicles and robotics.
As part of that, the company has found itself at the center of competition between the U.S. and China, with advanced AI chips regarded as strategically important technology and the company able to sell in both markets. The company's manufacturing of advanced semiconductors also falls within national security concerns, with Washington, D.C., not wanting China to have access to the components.
Nvidia said its investigation would look into Huang potentially being the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
According to the Times , his relationship with a woman the outlet identified as Alice Huang had raised concerns within the U.S. government earlier this year, after it was revealed she had been sharing information with the government in Beijing.
U.S. officials briefed on the matter told the Times the woman was recruited to collect intelligence on Huang, as part of an effort by China to gain more information on American AI chips. Intelligence agencies in the U.S. have been investigating why Beijing had taken such an interest in Huang and Nvidia in particular.
On Thursday, three GOP leaders in the House of Representatives requested Huang appear before them for a closed-door briefing on the matter.
House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast of Florida, Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar of Michigan, and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford of Arkansas said the reports had raised "significant national security concerns," in a joint statement.
"The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress," the three Representatives said. "It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk."
In a note sent to Nvidia staff Sunday, Huang apologized to his wife and family, saying he had let them down. He also issued an apology to those he works with.
"To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me," Huang wrote. "Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence."
The company's board said it had no reason to believe any national security or Nvidia secrets had been shared.

articles.title_orig: Iran gives US two-day diplomacy ultimatum
articles.title_zh: Iran gives US two-day diplomacy ultimatum
articles.content_orig:
Trump still considering new assault on Iran nuclear sites – though threats less credible after Vance remarks
Qatar, the lead mediator in the US-Iran conflict, is seeking to persuade Tehran to allow UN nuclear weapons inspectors to visit Iran’s bombed nuclear sites, including those housing the country’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium.
Iran would not be required to make any commitment that the stockpile would be removed from the country, with other options on the table, including reducing the uranium content by down-blending it.
Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani, the emir of Qatar, spoke to Donald Trump about the proposal, the emir’s office said on Friday without revealing the call’s contents.
The state news agency said the emir “emphasised the importance of continuing dialogue and embracing diplomacy as a means of resolving disputes, preventing further escalation in the region”.
Trump is still considering whether to mount a further assault on Iranian nuclear sites, though the credibility of his threats is weaker inside Iran after his vice-president, JD Vance, said the war itself, and not just its cost to American consumers, was critical to the collapse of the Republican vote in the US midterms .
Under the Qatar proposal, the US would immediately lift the naval blockade on Iran in the strait of Hormuz and release a portion of the $8bn (£6bn) of its frozen assets. In return, Iran would agree to visits by International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors to its bombed nuclear facilities, based on a previous abandoned agreement that had been reached in Cairo in September 2025.
Iran would open the strait of Hormuz on the second day, via a route it has already negotiated with Oman that they would jointly lodge with the International Maritime Organisation (IMO).
Iran has multiple other preconditions for opening the strait including ending the war in Lebanon, a withdrawal of US forces from the Iranian coastline, a commitment to lift some economic sanctions, and agreement to pay war reparations. The sequencing of these commitments has been at the heart of the mediation.
In the memorandum of understanding, a $300bn reconstruction and development fund was to be set up to help Iran recover economically, but it was never clear exactly how this proposal was to be funded.
Iran, in a triumphalist mood after Trump’s election wipeout, has been wary of allowing the UN nuclear inspectors back into the country, claiming it had lost faith in Rafael Grossi, the head of the inspectorate.
Tehran claims Grossi betrayed his duty to uphold the nuclear non-proliferation treaty, by failing to criticise the US for bombing Iran’s nuclear sites. It fears that material gathered by the inspectors would be handed over as targeting data to the Americans and Israelis.
In the parallel talks on opening the strait, Oman’s foreign minister, Badr Albusaidi, spoke again to Iran about the future of the strait administration including the agreed route, the extent to which the agreement is temporary and the need to register the proposal with the IMO, either as a bilateral agreement or a joint regional proposal.
Oman has a long-term proposal for the administration of the strait compliant with the law of the sea in that shipping companies would be charged only for services, and not tolls.
Amir Hayat Moqaddam, the deputy chair of the Iranian parliament’s national security and foreign policy committee, told the Iranian Students’ News Agency (ISNA) on Tuesday that ships from four countries – China, India, Qatar and Iraq – were allowed to pass through the strategic waterway.
The exemptions served mutual interests, he said, adding that Iran charged Indian and Chinese vessels transit fees while allowing Qatari ships to pass free of charge. Medicine was received from India, while China provided political support.
It is reported that of the 10.23m barrels a day of Gulf crude that passed through the strait in October, about 42% went to China and 13% to India, said Muyu Xu, a senior crude oil analyst at the analytics firm Kpler.
The navy of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said two “violating” oil tankers attempting to pass through an unauthorised route in the eastern sector of the strait of Hormuz had collided with mines and caught fire.
The IRGC said the two tankers had turned off their navigation and identification systems and that the attempted crossing was with the support of US military forces.

articles.title_orig: Cruise ship pianist rescued after nine hours treading water miles from shore
articles.title_zh: Cruise ship pianist rescued after nine hours treading water miles from shore
articles.content_orig:
Man taken to hospital after falling off Royal Caribbean ship in Pacific Ocean, with Coast Guard investigating incident
A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two Newport Beach, California , fishermen discovered him treading water in the Pacific Ocean nearly 20 miles (32km) offshore on Friday.
The unidentified man was taken to the hospital after the rescue, according to the US Coast Guard, which is now investigating how he went overboard from the cruise ship.
Authorities believe the man may have been in the ocean for approximately nine hours before he was spotted by Sean Norton and Grant Garrett, who were returning from a fishing trip near Catalina Island.
The two fishermen had spent the morning fishing for marlin when their trip took an unexpected turn. By noon, they had pulled the stranded man from the water.
“I’m like, ‘Yeah, it’s a human being. Stop the boat; let’s get all of our lines in,” Garrett told CBS News , recalling the moment the boat’s captain first saw the man in the water.
The fishermen quickly worked together to bring the man onboard. Once the man regained his composure, Garrett said he identified himself as a pianist onboard Royal Caribbean’s 14-deck cruise ship, the “Ovation of the Seas.”
According to Norton, the rescued crew member had few words to describe what he had just experienced. “The only thing he said to me was, ‘Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,’” Norton said.
After the rescue, the fishing crew issued an emergency maritime call, prompting Newport Beach lifeguards to respond and provide assistance. Battalion chief Adam Yacenda said the man was found approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, according to CBS, or “pretty much in the middle of the ocean”.
Despite the extended time spent in the water, Norton believes unusually warm ocean temperatures may have played a significant role in the man’s survival.
“You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water’s 76 degrees,” Norton said. “A different year, no way he makes it.”
The circumstances surrounding the crew member’s fall from the cruise ship remain under investigation by the Coast Guard. Royal Caribbean Group acknowledged the incident and said it is assisting the employee following the ordeal.
In a statement to CBS, a company spokesperson said: “We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share.”

articles.title_orig: Collision between 2 trains in Egypt kills 7 and injures at least 125
articles.title_zh: Collision between 2 trains in Egypt kills 7 and injures at least 125
articles.content_orig:
At least seven people were killed and 112 people injured after two trains collided in Egypt on Sunday, the country’s health ministry said.
Several carriages were derailed after one train collided with the rear of another between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Giza, near the capital Cairo, the Egyptian National Railways Authority said in a statement.
Dozens of ambulances were dispatched to transport the injured to nearby hospitals, while cranes were deployed to remove the wreckage after traffic on the railroad was disrupted, Egyptian authorities said.
Among the dozens injured in the collision, 45 people have been discharged from nearby hospitals after their condition improved, according to the health ministry.
The Egyptian railway system, the oldest in Africa and the Middle East, has a long history of deadly accidents.
In 2019, a train lost control while approaching Cairo’s main station in Ramses Square, igniting a fire that killed 25 people. Another accident in 2017 occurred on the way to Alexandria, when a train derailed and collided head-on with another train, killing more than 40 people.
Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi ordered an investigation into the Giza collision on Sunday, according to statement on his official Facebook page. He also offered his “sincere condolences” to those killed.
This story has been updated.
CNN’s Sana Noor Haq contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Akai MPC is moving toward an open platform, and the first step is here
articles.title_zh: Akai MPC is moving toward an open platform, and the first step is here
articles.content_orig:
SYNTH ANATOMY uses affiliation & partner programs (big red buttons) to finance a part of the activity. If you use these, you support the website. Thanks! Reading Time: 3 minutes
The Akai MPC is moving toward an open platform, and the first step is here with a GitHub repository and insights into the hardware used in the standalone MPCs.
On October 28 , Akai announced it is making its MPC Sample hardware sampler open source—as is the upcoming SampleKey . This sparked a great deal of discussion. I believe it’s actually the biggest one this year.
Then, last Friday, news broke that Akai plans to unveil 22 new products at NAMM 2027 , many of them open to experiment with. Today, Akai or inMusic has taken its first step to open its MPC platform for creators – and it’s not just the MPC Sample
Akai hasn’t made an official announcement yet, but inMusic has opened an official GitHub repository managed by Pete Goodliffe, CTO (Chief Technical Officer) and lead developer of the MPC platform. Bang, it happened, or?!
It contains the open-source components required by the licenses under which they are distributed. It does not, however, mean that inMusic or Akai has published the MPC OS as open source. This could help developers understand the underlying software environment.
Interestingly, this new repository suggests they are about to open not just the MPC Sample, but the entire MPC lineup . Plus, they’ll add the SampleKey when it is released.
Thanks for your interest in the open source software used by inMusic Brands. We are happy to comply with the requirements of the open source libraries and projects in use in our products.
This repo contains archives of the open source code for the Linux environment in our products. You will find very few changes against the upstream projects here; we aim to submit all relevant patches back up to the mainstream projects.
You can now find three different Akai MPC open releases on GitHub:
With this upcoming move, the long-running “Hakai OS” project —for example, which enables jailbreaking the MPC hardware—doesn’t go underground; it becomes an official project.
The first step in opening Pandora’s box has been taken, and a new era for the MPCs is about to start.  A game-changer, as you might say. The first step has been taken; the others will probably follow soon.
We will soon see numerous new projects that will transform the hardware, both the standalones and MPC Sample, into entirely new instruments.  If the community embraces this, inMusic’s plan will have succeeded.
As they communicated yesterday, they want to give creators hardware for making music and also to experiment with their own crafted or AI-generated tools. We have some exciting months ahead, during which it remains to be seen what exactly will come our way.
The Akai MPC framework and its components are now open source and available on GitHub.
More information here: Akai Pro / GitHub

Sweet! No more paying for basic features like the clip launcher. 🙂
We aren’t quite there yet. For now, the MPC framework and components—the foundation for the MPC OS—are free and open for custom operating systems.
What do you mean that the OS is not open? I don’t understand the difference 😅😅 Does it mean that user OS can be installed, but the original OS can’t be changed? But then you said that unofficial plugins can be used, which I assume involves the original OS 😵‍💫😵‍💫
The MPCs are based on a Linux foundation with added components, such as the controls. So, the “bed” on which the MPC OS lies. This is now open and people can make their own OS on this base. The MPC OS, the operation system, isn’t open-source yet and not if it will be. We will see this
Akai’s “open source” release is not what many people think it is
Akai has published source code for the MPC G1 line (MPC Live II, One, X, Force and others), and the first reaction I saw was: “Great, now we can write our own synths for the MPC.” I don’t think that’s what this is.
I went through the repository. It’s a license-compliance archive, the kind a company has to publish when its devices ship GPL and LGPL software. It holds 72 source packages: a custom Linux kernel, systemd, ALSA, busybox and similar parts. It doesn’t contain the MPC application, the plugin host, the AIR instruments or any SDK.
I also looked into the MPC 3 desktop software installed on my machine. Its bundled plugins are only skins and presets. The sound engines are compiled into the app. It does contain an embedded Lua engine, but it looks like an internal automation tool for reading and comparing UI state, not a scripting feature for users. I found no way to load your own scripts. That’s my reading of the files, not a statement from Akai.
Akai’s own support page also says third-party plugins can’t be loaded in standalone mode.
So what does the release give us? A look at the Linux foundation under the hardware, which is useful for researchers. Custom synths on a Live II it does not give us. If that changes, it will need an official plugin format from Akai.
I use an MPC Live II as part of my dawless rig, so I’d love to be wrong about this.
Exactly what I wrote: the MPC OS isn’t open-source, but the foundation it sits on is. So the bed on which people can code/vibe-code their own custom OS. I’m not sure if Akai will open-source the O.
So why use such a clickbaity title then? Oh right, because that’s what we do in marketing these days.
The framework and its components are open source! You can create your own custom firmware for it. So the MPC hardware is open source.
The title isn’t misleading or clickbait because it says “Akai MPC is now open-source”. It doesn’t say “Akai MPC OS is now open-source”.
Ok, let me try again. Yes, you didn’t write “Akai MPC OS is now open-source”. However, in the current trend of people modding firmware, and companies picking up to the trend of open sourcing their whole firmware (including actual features like sampler and reverbs etc.), this is what a typical user would kind of expect when the title says “Akai MPC is now open-source”.
We must return to reading actual articles instead of just titles so they understand what it is actually about.
So what is so good about it?
I had a look through the Gen 2 files. They’re mostly the standard Linux parts Akai has to publish to stay compliant with open-source licenses (kernel, bootloader, system libraries), not the MPC software itself. Still useful for tinkerers, but it doesn’t unlock anything or add plugin support on its own.
I believe this is just the required source disclosures from open source components they use, not the intended framework for anyone to make their own software / run additional things on the devices. This doesn’t, for instance, compile or run on devices without AKAI’s signing keys.
It is a great step and gives some nice disclosure as to the hardware layout, but I think you may have jumped the gun a bit on this one.
I made it clearer, and as usual with my articles, I’ll update and extend them with new information as it becomes available. This is the first step in the new “open” era of the MPC.
Yup, hopefully more steps soon!
Open platform, not open source.  Big difference and honestly much better option.
so they published the open source libraries they used on their mach

articles.title_orig: Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and arrives in Milei’s Argentina for the most fraught stop of his tour
articles.title_zh: Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and arrives in Milei’s Argentina for the most fraught stop of his tour
articles.content_orig:
On Sunday morning, Pope Leo XIV greeted the faithful of the parish of Saint Therese in Juanicó in Montevideo, Uruguay, expressing his closeness to them.
The Holy Father said, âYou may not know this, but I am truly very happy to share this brief moment with you at the parish of Saint Thérèse. It is the first parish in Uruguay to be dedicated to her after her canonisation.â
During his stop in Juanicó, the Pope entered the parish church for a moment of prayer and recollection and subsequently greeted the approximately 2,000 faithful gathered in the parish courtyard.
The Pope shared a personal family experience of devotion to the patron saint of the parish.
âIn my family, especially with my father, we had a great devotion to Saint Thérèse,â he said.
The Pope, who was on his way to the town of Florida to celebrate Mass for the feast of Our Lady of the Thirty-Three, marking the conclusion of his Apostolic Visit to the country, reflected on God's constant closeness to us.
âThis is a moment of devotion, a moment of thanksgiving, a moment to recognise that God's grace and God's love are always with us, and that God accompanies us at every moment," he said, stressing this remains the case "whether in happy times or when we suffer, when we are experiencing illness, pain or so many difficulties.â
Before leaving, the Holy Father imparted his blessing upon the faithful.
âLet us ask the Lord to bless each one of you and your families. For those who have brought rosaries or other devotional objects, we bless them as well at this time,â he prayed.
Finally, he prayed, let us ask the Lord "to help us all grow in faith, to live our faith courageously, and not to be afraid to say: âI am a Christian, I am Catholic, I believe in Jesus Christ.â Jesus has given us a life that teaches us, in turn, to live by serving others, walking together in unity and seeking the presence of God, sharing with everyone the joy of being Christians.â

articles.title_orig: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
articles.title_zh: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
articles.content_orig:
A view through the destroyed walls of a kindergarten shows a large bomb crater and a damaged residential apartment building following a missile attack in Kyiv, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Dan Bashakov/AP hide caption
European officials will turn up for the U.S.-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine in the United Arab Emirates this week, France's foreign minister said Sunday, days after the Kremlin had insisted there could be no role for European powers at the meeting.
"France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard," Jean-Noël Barrot told French radio. He did not say who would represent Paris, or whether French or other European officials would take part directly in negotiations, or simply observe.
The meetings, which are set to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, had previously been presented as a three-way session between Washington, Moscow and Kyiv.
The Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had earlier ruled out a European role, saying the trilateral format had already been agreed.
Talking to a Russian news channel on Friday, he accused European governments of failing to decide who speaks for them, while acknowledging that security talks would at some point require Europe's involvement.
On Thursday, President Trump met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev and said a coming agreement was "going to involve more than Ukraine," adding he could even say it "might involve all of Europe."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CNN on Friday that he had not been given details of the agreement Trump had referenced, and warned: "For me, it's not simple, and it can be dangerous." He invoked the 1945 Yalta conference, where Allied leaders settled Europe's division without the involvement of several affected countries.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, right, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attend a press conference in Berlin, Germany, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Ebrahim Noroozi/AP hide caption
This will be the fourth round of talks between the two warring nations brokered by the Trump administration, and the first since those in Geneva this February. Earlier U.S.-brokered meetings have made little progress, and the chances of a breakthrough have been reduced as the Trump administration focused on its war with Iran.
Moscow confirmed it would return to the negotiating table only following a visit by U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg in October. Those talks saw Putin announce the release of an American prisoner from a Russian jail — an apparent Kremlin gesture to President Trump's earlier lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Ukraine was vehemently opposed to the fuel sales — arguing they helped replenish Moscow's war chest.
Witkoff has said the agenda for these latest talks will include postwar security arrangements and de-escalation of the conflict and humanitarian issues, shortly after Melania Trump helped broker a limited ceasefire that allowed humanitarian aid to enter a town inside Russian-occupied Ukraine.
Russia's delegation will again be led by Vladimir Medinsky, a hardline Putin aide who has participated in most talks with Ukraine since the unsuccessful first set of discussions all the way back in March 2022.
For the first time, these talks will also include Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, as well as Yury Zhigarlovsky, a deputy head of the General Staff's operations directorate, alongside military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov.
This more senior lineup could indicate that Moscow is readier than before to address thorny political and military questions. But the U.S. think tankInstitute for the Study of War suggested some of those same Russian officials have in fact previously sought to slow down previous talks or push harder on Moscow's demands.
The gaps between the two countries remain substantial. Russia has demanded that Ukraine give up large parts of its territory and renounce NATO membership. Zelenskyy has repeatedly insisted any security commitments should be clearly spelled out, including who would act, and how, if Russia attacked again.
Russian President Vladimir Putin, right, interacts with people at the monument to merchant Kuzma Minin and Prince Dmitry Pozharsky, leaders of the struggle against foreign invaders in 1612, in Red Square in Moscow, Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, during National Unity Day celebrations. Yuri Kochetkov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin hide caption
Some analysts expect little. In an op-ed for the Atlantic Council think tank, the former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine John Herbst argued that Putin had rejected every U.S. proposal Kyiv accepted and preferred participating in peace talks than pursuing actual peace. "Perhaps the only outcome of the talks," he wrote, "will be to agree to another round."
The meetings in the United Arab Emirates also follow Democrats' midterm victories, which Zelenskyy said could improve Ukraine's chances of more U.S. aid.
Russia, too, may be looking to push for the Trump administration's outlines of a Ukraine deal — before a Democratic-controlled Congress arrives come January.
Also hovering over the talks — the prospect of Trump, Xi, and Putin gathering for a trilateral meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China later this month. While details remain murky, all sides have confirmed discussions are underway.
And as officials travel to Abu Dhabi to talk peace, the war has raged on regardless.
Zelenskyy said Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv area overnight Saturday, with only four intercepted, accusing Moscow of treating diplomacy "as a form of aggression."
In southern Ukraine, the death toll from a guided-bomb strike Monday on an aid distribution site in Komyshuvakha rose to at least 55.

articles.title_orig: UN agency for Palestinian refugees eyeing major restructuring
articles.title_zh: UN agency for Palestinian refugees eyeing major restructuring
articles.content_orig:
The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) is considering a major restructuring that could see thousands of its employees laid off and some of its responsibilities transferred to other bodies, including US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace, according to multiple media reports citing diplomatic sources.
The reported proposal is spearheaded by UNRWA’s acting commissioner-general, Christian Saunders, and comes as the agency faces a severe financial crisis.
Trump’s Board of Peace (BoP), established under the framework endorsed by the UN Security Council in November 2025, is tasked with overseeing Gaza’s transitional governance, reconstruction, economic recovery, and coordination of humanitarian assistance.
The BoP has been explicit in its opposition to the UN agency set up for Palestinian refugees only, making it clear in a July 1 statement that “UNRWA has no place in the new Gaza .”
“We are turning the page on the complex of perpetual aid dependency and conflict. The people of Gaza deserve better,” the BoP said in a social media post on September 25.
In the same post, the BoP said it would “only work with trusted partners who will deliver for the people of Gaza and contribute to a de-radicalized Strip. UNRWA fails on those litmus tests.”
However, the Associated Press reported, also on September 25, that BoP representatives have held several private meetings with UNRWA officials. A BoP official acknowledged that some of the agency’s programs and vetted employees could continue if they were effective and accountable, while maintaining that the UN body’s institutional role was ending.
UN Watch’s Hillel Neuer posted last week that there is a plan to unravel UNRWA, which has long faced criticism from Israel, the United States, and UN Watch over allegations of links between some of its employees and terrorist organizations such as Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) – including participating in October 7 and holding hostages.
According to Israel Hayom , which cited Arab and Western diplomatic sources, discussions have taken place about transferring some of UNRWA’s responsibilities to the BoP and other bodies.
Some of the agency’s remit could reportedly also be transferred to the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the West Bank.
The reported proposal was presented by Saunders at a meeting of UNRWA’s Advisory Commission, with the agency’s financial difficulties cited as a central reason for the restructuring. Saunders told Anadolu Agency on October 20 that the agency’s deficit stood at approximately $70 million.
“If we don’t receive money in the very near future, I will have to take some regrettable actions in order to ensure that we’re able to finish the year and to pay our staff salaries,” Saunders warned.
The head of the Arab Staff Union in Gaza, Mustafa Al-Ghoul, told the Mondoweiss anti-Zionist news site last week that UNRWA had dismissed around 1,000 staff in Gaza and let 2,000 retire without replacing them, leaving roughly 10,500.
Saunders gave the same figures in the Anadolu Agency interview, saying “We have 10,500 personnel on the ground [in the Gaza Strip].”
He also expressed support for the broader international framework for Gaza, saying: “ US President Trump ’s 20-point plan, UN Security Council Resolution 2803, the Board of Peace, and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza – we are completely behind these efforts.”
Separately, Swiss French-language daily newspaper Le Temps published an investigation last week saying that Saunders plans for UNRWA to close its doors “within four or five years.” This has not yet been independently verified.
Under the UN-backed framework, the BoP is to exercise transitional authority in Gaza until the PA has completed its reform program and can securely and effectively resume control. In the meantime, the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza is intended to serve as an interim technocratic administration.
Currently, UNRWA purports to be assisting more than 1.7 million Palestinians in Gaza, providing healthcare through 11 centers, schooling for approximately 300,000 children, and drinking water for around 820,000 people.
It also says it provides essential services to nearly six million Palestinian refugees across Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, and the West Bank.

articles.title_orig: China's half-price Rolls-Royce: Yangwang Altior is a lavish alternative to a Phantom limo
articles.title_zh: China's half-price Rolls-Royce: Yangwang Altior is a lavish alternative to a Phantom limo
articles.content_orig:
By ROB HULL, MOTORING EDITOR
Updated: 13:34 EDT, 8 November 2026
We've had the Temu Range Rover; now there's an AliExpress Roller.
Chinese brand Yangwang, a spin-off from electric car giant BYD, has unveiled a new battery-powered luxury vehicle called the Altior, and it bears a striking resemblance to the iconic British Rolls-Royce Phantom limousine – but for around half the price.
At 5.6m long, with a vast bonnet and grille, rear-hinged coach doors, a palatial interior and umbrellas stowed inside the door panels, there's no hiding which ostentatious motor it has firmly set its sights on.
Altior means 'higher' in Latin, with the car 'expressing an ambition to elevate the experience of luxury through cultural depth, personal expression and technological progress', Yangwang says.
Just 399 are going to be produced and reports in China suggest pre-orders are available from 2million yuan, which equates to around £230,000.
That puts it closer to the £250,000 Rolls-Royce Ghost than the flagship £450,000 Phantom, though that's before taking into account heavily subsidised pricing in China's domestic market.
Its global premiere in Abu Dhabi this weekend comes just days after car registration figures revealed that Jaecoo's 'Temu Range Rover' 7 SUV was the UK's best-selling new model for a second successive month .
The runaway success of the Range Rover Velar lookalike is the clearest sign yet that Chinese brands are coming for the old guard of established luxury carmakers. And with the Altior, it appears not even Rolls-Royce is safe.
This is the new Yangwang Altior limousine - a luxury Rolls-Royce Phantom rival from Chinese EV giant, BYD
While the Rolls-Royce Phantom and Ghost feature a gutsy 6.75-litre twin-turbocharged V12 petrol engine, the Yangwang Altior is a far greener proposition.
It uses a version of the quad-electric motor setup deployed in the Chinese firm's other models, the U8 SUV and U9 supercar. That's likely to produce more than 1,000bhp and will allow it to perform a tank turn , rotating each wheel independently to spin the vehicle on its own axis.
Providing the energy for the e-motors is BYD's second-generation Blade Battery technology.
As such, it's claimed to be capable of travelling more than 621 miles on a full charge. However, this is based on Chinese efficiency tests that are historically a shade more optimistic than Europe's cycle, which would be closer to 520 miles.
The battery is compatible with BYD's network of Flash Charging stations, of which there are 10,000 already in China and a promise to install 300 here in the UK .
The ground-breaking devices can deliver up to 1,500kW of power and top up a battery pack from 10 to 70 per cent charge in as little as five minutes, before reaching full charge in less than ten.
That's not all in terms of technological advances.
The Yangwang boasts a suite of chassis tech that means it can float if there are flash floods or the driver 'accidentally enters water'. And it can continue tracking in a straight line when one of the tyres suffers a high-speed blowout on the motorway.
The Altior also taps into BYD's God's Eye A assisted-driving system, which includes parking-space-to-parking-space navigation assistance. This enables the car to drive itself from one car park to another, even when they are hundreds of miles apart.
The suspension is clever too. The brand's DiSus active body control system uses cameras to read the road ahead and adjusts damping in real time, meaning occupants won't feel potholes or changes in road surfaces while stretched out in the back.
Altior means 'higher' in Latin, as BYD's spin-off Yangwang looks to enter a more opulent market with its latest model. And it certain strikes a resemblance to the Rolls-Royce Phantom
Squint slightly and there's no mistaking the Rolls-Royce-inspired silhouette.
The elongated bonnet, despite there being no 12-cylinder combustion engine lurking beneath it, and the glitzy upright grille are trademarks of the 122-year-old British marque.
The Altior's front end is described as a 'masterpiece of high jewellery'.
'Meticulous selection, polishing and individual placement create a composition that responds to changing light, revealing new depth and brilliance as the viewpoint moves,' the Chinese manufacturer says.
Its lights are a little special too, featuring 12 individual elements that rotate from the outside to the centre to create a 'ceremonial welcome' when the owner approaches.
At 5.6m long, the Altior (pictured left) is 5.5cm longer than the Ghost and 16cm shorter than the Phantom (pictured right)
Like all Roller limousines, the Chinese Yangwang has rear-hinged coach doors
Twenty-one-inch wheels are standard, with the dish-style monoblock design bearing more than a passing resemblance to the disc rims available on a Phantom
Is it time for European luxury car makers to fear China’s fast-rising electric rivals?
At 5.6m long, the Altior is 5.5cm longer than the Ghost and 16cm shorter than the Phantom.
However, the Yangwang's other dimensions, including a width of 2m, a height of almost 1.6m and a wheelbase of 3.5m, are almost like-for-like with the bigger of the two Rolls-Royces.
Twenty-one-inch wheels are standard, with the dish-style monoblock design bearing more than a passing resemblance to the disc rims available on a Phantom.
The doors also open in the fashion for which Rolls-Royce is famed, providing generous access to the opulent interior.
The finely crafted bespoke umbrellas hidden in each door panel, much like those in a Rolls-Royce, are said to be inspired by the circular wooden roof of the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests at China's Temple of Heaven complex.
The cockpit is the least Roller-like part of the car. While the British luxury firm attempts to conceal tech for a traditional look, the Yangwang has a dashboard-wide high-definition screen
Exactly like Rolls-Royces, though, the Chinese limo has bespoke, hand-crafted umbrellas hidden in a compartment within the doors
Step inside and the cabin – dubbed a 'private lounge' – is awash with only the highest-quality materials.
These include hammer-tested metal switches, pure-wool floor mats, real-wood veneers, 48 jewellery-inspired control buttons and semi-aniline leather upholstery.
The designers have even mounted polished yellow jade gemstones inside the vertical air vents, while the silk-embroidered door panels feature cloud and thunder-pattern motifs.
The cockpit itself looks a little less Rolls-Royce-esque, even if it does feature a chrome-rimmed steering wheel wrapped in beautifully finished leather.
While the British car maker generally tries to subtly conceal much of its modern technology up front, the Yangwang has a dashboard-spanning digital glass display. This incorporates an instrument cluster with classic-style digital dials and an enormous infotainment screen featuring a laptop-style taskbar of icons.
But it's the rear compartment that well-heeled customers will want to know about.
The cabin is as palatial as you'd expect from a Rolls-Royce or Bentley limo. It boasts aviation-style zero-gravity seats, real-wood veneers and 48 jewellery-inspired control buttons
There's a fridge in the rear and in the front, two champagne flute holders and a control panel that means you won't have to converse with your chauffeur at all
There's plenty of artistry too. Silk-embroidered door panels feature cloud and thunder-pattern motifs
The four-seat layout is almost perfectly symmetrical and 'gives each occupant a clearly defined personal space' where the owner in the back can feel entirely separate from Jeeves behind the wheel by elevating a divider between them.
Owners won't need to ask their chauffeur for anything, either.
Rear occupants can access all key functions through the central console, including lowering the front passenger seat at the touch of a button to provide an uninterrupted view ahead.
The rear chairs are 'aviation-style zero-gravity seats' that provide a 'deeply relaxed'

articles.title_orig: More Than 3,000 Tarantulas Found in Smugglers’ Socks at Peru Airport
articles.title_zh: More Than 3,000 Tarantulas Found in Smugglers’ Socks at Peru Airport
articles.content_orig:
Three suitcases’ worth of the spiders were on their way to Germany, where they could fetch an estimated €1.5m
More than 3,000 tarantulas were seized at an airport in Lima on their way to Germany, Peruvian authorities said.
The spiders were hidden inside dirty socks contained in three suitcases carried by two Germans and a Polish citizen, the National Forestry and Wildlife Service (SERFOR) told Agence France-Presse on Thursday.
They were spotted after agents noticed some unusual wriggling inside the luggage during a routine customs inspection at Jorge Chávez international airport. “We noticed that some of them were moving. There were small ones and large ones,” said Cora Suarez, a SERFOR wildlife control technician.
One tarantula can sell for about €500 ($560) in Europe, Suarez said, meaning the wildlife trafficking scheme would be potentially worth €1.5m for just one trip.
The hidden arachnids, which came from several regions of Peru, were found in varying stages of development, from eggs and hatchlings to adults, Suarez said.
The Europeans accused of smuggling the tarantulas were detained by police specialising in environmental crimes and will face criminal proceedings, SERFOR said.
Illegal wildlife trafficking is a highly lucrative criminal activity that generates around $20bn annually worldwide, according to Interpol.
Such trafficking is among the primary causes of the loss of biodiversity on the planet.

articles.title_orig: Trump unveils 'Iron Gate' task force against Iran as Saudis launch deadly strikes on Houthi rebels
articles.title_zh: Trump unveils 'Iron Gate' task force against Iran as Saudis launch deadly strikes on Houthi rebels
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump said Sunday that a renewed war with Iran is “highly unlikely” if Tehran makes progress toward a nuclear agreement and reopens the Strait of Hormuz — while warning that the U.S. has 38 Iranian bridges in its sights.
“It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump told CNN .
Trump said military action would probably not be necessary, but warned that the U.S. is prepared to strike Iran again.
“The answer is highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary,” Trump said. “They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301% inflation. Highly unlikely it will be necessary. I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them.”
Trump added that it is “highly unlikely” he would have to order another attack.
“They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off,” he warned.
“We’re ready for it. I’ve got three aircraft carriers here. The other one just arrived. We have three. They’re fully locked and loaded,” Trump continued.
He also said the U.S. could destroy dozens of bridges in Iran within hours.
“We have 38 bridges in our sight that we can knock down in literally one hour,” Trump said. “They’ll all be down.”
“I don’t want to do that because, essentially, it’ll take 10 years to rebuild them,” he added. “I don’t like ripping down bridges. And the hardest thing to build is a bridge. It takes years, and I’m a good builder.”
Diplomatic activity across the Middle East has continued since Thursday, with Qatar mediating efforts to advance talks between Washington and Tehran
Yemen's armed forces said Sunday they carried out nearly 1,000 strikes, including dozens of air and drone attacks, in a major offensive that reportedly left hundreds of militia fighters dead, wounded or on the run.
Brig. Gen. Majed Abdullah Al-Nuzaili, a spokesman for Yemen's armed forces, announced the operations Sunday in a post on X .
The forces said they carried out 19 airstrikes on the Marib, Taiz and Tur al-Bahah fronts, targeting militia positions, troop concentrations and vehicles. Drones conducted another 29 strikes on combat positions, vehicles, weapons and other militia assets.
“Field artillery and rocket launchers also carried out 944 strikes on militia concentrations and reinforcements, firing positions, fortifications, barricades, and sniper positions,” Al-Nuzaili added.
The strikes killed, wounded or forced approximately 267 militia commanders and fighters to flee the battlefield, according to the statement. The attacks also destroyed or damaged 97 military vehicles.
Yemen's army also released footage of a Houthi ambush carried out by troops it described as “the heroes of the 1st Emergency Division forces.”
President Donald Trump on Sunday touted Washington’s new U.S. military task force aimed at choking off Iran's weapons supply routes, as it ramps up pressure through its maritime blockade.
“Task Force Iron Gate is in full force and effect in the Islamic Republic of Iran ,” Trump said on Truth Social.
“Coupled with history’s greatest Naval Blockade, very little gets into, or out of, Iran!” he added.
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the formation of Task Force Iron Gate on Saturday, saying the roughly 20-person team will be based in Tampa, Florida, and work to disrupt the movement of weapons, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.
The U.S. Treasury Department asked that Iraq shut down all but two of its border crossings with Iran as part of a drive to isolate Tehran, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said Sunday, according to Reuters .
“There are many official and unofficial border crossings with Iran, and closing all of them would be difficult and would affect our economy.
“The Americans are still demanding the closure of the crossings, and we are currently in discussions with them,” Hussein said in an interview with Al Jazeera.
The development came as U.S. Central Command ( CENTCOM ) moved to close off Tehran’s overland corridors militarily, directing the establishment of Task Force Iron Gate on Nov. 7.
Adm. Brad Cooper said the initiative was to build on the “success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea” and would “further constrain Iran’s ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military.”
Iran's foreign minister issued a stark ultimatum to the White House on Sunday, warning that Tehran's forces would "rain down hell" if Washington chooses war over a diplomatic proposal aimed at ending the war.
“American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own,” Abbas Araghchi said of the latest proposal sent to Washington.
“Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results,” he said on X .
“Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell,” he warned.
According to Reuters , Araghchi also said Sunday that the midterm results had temporarily stalled mediation efforts aimed at securing a deal between Tehran and Washington.
Araghchi told Iranian state television that Tehran would have to wait for mediators to resume diplomatic efforts.
Iran submitted a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar on Thursday, a senior Iranian official told Reuters.

articles.title_orig: King leads solemn Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
articles.title_zh: King leads solemn Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
articles.content_orig:
King Charles III led the nation in a solemn two-minute silence on Remembrance Sunday in London to honour veterans who had died in conflict.
On a stone-grey autumn morning, he laid a wreath at the Cenotaph in Whitehall before a march-past by 10,000 armed forces veterans.
That included a shrinking number of World War Two veterans, with 12 taking part this year, including 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who described it as a "very emotional day".
Meanwhile, the number of former prime ministers reached a record high, with nine lined up to lay wreaths, while Andy Burnham attended for the first time as the current occupant of No 10 Downing Street.
And for the first time, the leader of Reform UK, Nigel Farage, had enough MPs in Parliament to qualify to lay a wreath alongside other major party leaders.
The Prince of Wales and the Princess Royal were among royals in attendance, along with military chiefs, senior politicians, diplomats and faith leaders, watched by big crowds squeezed behind railings along Whitehall.
Queen Camilla and the Princess of Wales watched from a balcony above the Cenotaph in the Foreign Office.
Among the flags on the roof of that Whitehall building was the Ukrainian blue and yellow. It went up when Russia invaded and four years later it is now visibly frayed - a reminder of the length of that war and of current threats.
At 11:00 GMT, as the first strike of Big Ben echoed from the nearby Houses of Parliament, the big two-minute silence filled the usually frenetic streets, before the playing of the Last Post.
The King had his eyes closed, the crowds in Whitehall stopped for their own thoughts, in a rare moment of calm in the capital.
The poignant parade past the Cenotaph included representatives of about 340 different military and civilian groups, from the Royal Naval Association and the Royal Marines Association to Transport for London and the Royal National Lifeboat Institute.
Alongside those marching were flotillas of disability scooters and families helping veterans in wheelchairs.
Those who took part in WW2 are now increasingly frail - and there were 12 participants in the march-past compared to 20 last year. The oldest participant this year was aged 105.
Taking part for the first time was 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who had been part of the Land Army that had helped to feed the country at war.
She had joined the Land Army in 1940 as a 16-year-old, having lied about her age, and worked on a farm in Leicestershire.
"I feel very honoured to be taking part in the parade and to represent the Land Girls. I'm very excited, although a little apprehensive as I don't quite know what to expect," she said.
"I think it will be a very emotional day, bringing back memories of all those who didn't return home. It will be lovely to be there and remember them."
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the annual event was a time to "reflect on the selflessness and courage it takes to commit your life to protecting others".
He earlier announced that he wanted to tackle the problem of homelessness among ex-service personnel to "ensure that any veteran sleeping rough is offered appropriate accommodation before Christmas".
Mark Atkinson, the director general of the Royal British Legion, said: "As we come together on Remembrance Sunday, we pay tribute to all those who have served and sacrificed, from generations past to those still serving today."
Remembrance events took place across the country as thousands gathered to pay their respects to those who died in past conflicts.
First Minister of Scotland John Swinney placed a wreath at the Stone of Remembrance outside the City Chambers during an event in Edinburgh.
Veterans, military personnel and cadets also marched through the centres of British cities such as Manchester, Birmingham and Leeds.
A silent poppy drop was held as part of the Festival of Remembrance at Durham Cathedral while wreaths were laid at Canterbury Cathedral.
Separately, the Duke of Sussex was seen attending a Remembrance service in the market town of Brackley in Northamptonshire.
For more than a century, the national Remembrance event has been held around the Cenotaph.
The monument was built as a focal point for honouring those who had fought and died in World War One, including those who had no grave, and as a place to mourn for those families who might not be able to visit war cemeteries overseas.
The word "cenotaph" means "empty tomb" in Greek and it was designed by the architect Sir Edwin Lutyens in a simple, austere style, with no sense of triumphalism and with almost no decoration.
The monument had been originally built in 1919 as a temporary, plaster and wood structure. But it proved so popular with the public that it was replaced in 1920 with a permanent version, in the same design but in stone.
It was opened at 11:00 on 11 November 1920 by King George V. His great-grandson, Charles, was there again, on an overcast morning 106 years later, to continue paying respect.

articles.title_orig: Eisenkot open to Netanyahu joining Israel’s next government
articles.title_zh: Eisenkot open to Netanyahu joining Israel’s next government
articles.content_orig:
Israel’s opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot , the man officially tasked by President Isaac Herzog with trying to form the country’s next government, has said that he was open to including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his coalition lineup.
In a speech at Sunday’s ceremony in Herzog’s office in Jerusalem, Eisenkot suggested Netanyahu’s far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich was also welcome to join.
“If members of Likud and the Religious Zionist Party truly believe this is a time for unity, as they told the president, I cannot conceive of any reason why they would not support a government under my leadership and the principles I have presented,” Eisenkot said.
Eisenkot, who ran as Netanyahu’s main rival, has six weeks to form a new government. At the ceremony, Eisenkot said he will act in the interests of the public and represent all parts of Israeli society.
Herzog, meanwhile, warned that the country faced uncertainties after the November 3 midterm elections in the United States, which brought victories for several political figures critical of Israel and the US’s military support.
“The State of Israel needs a stable government,” Herzog said, pointing to the “new political reality” in the US.
Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and sat as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet for the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.
Despite this, Arab-led parties endorsed Eisenkot for the mandate to replace Netanyahu.
In Israel’s October 27 elections , Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.
Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with the Arab-led parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.
He could also form a government with fewer than 61 seats if he wins a parliamentary confidence vote.
“Netanyahu still has time to derail Gadi Eisenkot’s efforts to form a government and sabotage attempts to gain a vote of confidence,” said Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank.
“In the meantime, he remains caretaker prime minister. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would be the natural second in line to be tasked with forming a government. And if he fails, elections would then be called, and that would still allow Netanyahu to remain as caretaker.
“Many of Netanyahu’s critics say that is his aim. The big question in Israeli politics now is: does the opposition really want to get rid of Netanyahu? Or is the opposition to Palestinian Israelis in mainstream politics so strong that they’re willing to risk keeping Netanyahu in power by going back to the ballot box?”

articles.title_orig: Ghana Cancels 10 Passports Issued Illegally After Applicants Allegedly Paid Up To $29,000, Suspends Two Officials
articles.title_zh: Ghana Cancels 10 Passports Issued Illegally After Applicants Allegedly Paid Up To $29,000, Suspends Two Officials
articles.content_orig:
According to the ministry, one petitioner claimed to have paid $29,000 in 2023, while another alleged that he paid $5,000 in 2026 to members of the suspected criminal network.
Ghana’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has cancelled 10 service passports allegedly issued illegally to individuals who did not qualify for them after paying members of a suspected criminal syndicate, as part of an investigation into a passport-for-sale scheme dating back to 2023.
The ministry also announced the interdiction of two officials, including the Acting Director of Passports, Mahama Yahaya Amantana, and a junior Foreign Service Officer, Alhassan Sumani, over their alleged roles in the scheme.
In a statement issued in Accra on Sunday, November 8, 2026, the ministry said the investigation followed two petitions alleging irregularities in the issuance of service passports.
According to the ministry, one petitioner claimed to have paid $29,000 in 2023, while another alleged that he paid $5,000 in 2026 to members of the suspected criminal network.
The ministry said the first petition was received on October 8, 2026, prompting the Foreign Affairs Minister, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, to order the establishment of an investigative committee on October 13.
It said preliminary findings had confirmed that individuals who were not qualified to receive service passports obtained them after allegedly making illegal payments to a syndicate.
The 10 passports identified in the investigation were issued between January 2023 and August 2026.
Those affected include Richard Sakyi Apenteng and Augustina Agyei Boateng, whose passports were issued on January 3, 2023; Juliet Amankwa, issued on January 31, 2023; and Rebecca Agyeiwaa, issued on February 2, 2023.
Others are Prince Ahensah and Maybel Ahensah, whose passports were issued on May 28, 2026; Twumasi Francis Kwame, Gyabaah Anthony, Frederick Ennin and Bosompem Richard, whose passports were issued in August 2026.
The ministry said all 10 passports had been cancelled and could no longer be used.
It added that international partners had been notified of the cancellations, while efforts were underway to track down the beneficiaries, including two individuals who allegedly used the illegally obtained passports to travel in 2023.
The ministry identified Sumani as a key figure named in all the petitions, alleging that he operated as a passport-processing intermediary, commonly referred to as a “goro boy”, in 2023 before being recruited into the Foreign Service on November 29, 2024.
It said both Sumani and Amantana had been interdicted and referred to the Ghana Police Service for further investigations and possible prosecution.
The ministry also announced that Ambassador Mohammed Habib Idris, who served as Director of Passports during the period under investigation in 2023 and has since retired, would be investigated by security agencies.
It said he would be sanctioned if found culpable, just like the other officials under investigation.
“In the interest of fairness, impartiality and non-discrimination, the Director of Passports for the 2023 period in issue, Ambassador Mohammed Habib Idris, who is now retired, would also be investigated by the security services and sanctioned if found culpable just like his counterpart, Mr. Mahama Yahaya Amantana,” the statement said.
The ministry described the alleged operation as a sophisticated scheme that began before the current administration but said the investigation had exposed those behind it.
“It is apparent that this Service Passport For Sale Scheme was a sophisticated operation which predates the current administration, we are however glad that the masterminds have finally been exposed and rounded up due to our heightened diligence and zero tolerance for corruption,” it said.
The ministry also sought to distinguish the investigation from allegations involving diplomatic passports, insisting that there was no evidence that the country's diplomatic passports were being sold.
“The Ministry of Foreign Affairs wishes to state for the record that so far, no evidence has emerged that Ghana's Diplomatic Passports are being sold.
“For the avoidance of doubt, the matters under investigations are about Service Passports and not Diplomatic Passports,” the statement added.
The ministry said it was committed to ensuring that those responsible for the alleged irregularities were prosecuted, promising transparency and accountability throughout the investigation.
It also provided figures showing that 1,397 service passports were issued between 2009 and 2016, while 3,174 were issued between 2017 and 2024. A further 754 have been issued from 2025 to date.
For diplomatic passports, the ministry said 2,899 were issued between 2009 and 2016, 5,682 between 2017 and 2024, and 1,944 since 2025.
The statement also highlighted reforms introduced under President John Dramani Mahama, including the introduction of chip-embedded passports compliant with International Civil Aviation Organization standards, the establishment of passport application centres across all 16 regions, 24-hour operations, free courier delivery and an electronic tracking system.
It said the government had also reduced the passport application fee from GH₵500 to GH₵350 to make the document more affordable.
The ministry said the reforms were aimed at strengthening the credibility, security and efficiency of Ghana's passport administration system.

articles.title_orig: A Missionary Pope Faces a Chain Saw-Wielding Populist in Argentina
articles.title_zh: A Missionary Pope Faces a Chain Saw-Wielding Populist in Argentina
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina in the afternoon of Sunday, 8 November, for the second leg of his 12-day apostolic journey to three South American nations, following his visit to Uruguay. The journey will conclude in Peru.
The papal aircraft, an Aerolíneas Argentinas Boeing 737 MAX, covered the 365-kilometre journey from Montevideo to Buenos Aires in approximately one hour, flying over Uruguay and Argentina.
The Pope landed at Aeroparque Jorge Newbery International Airport in Buenos Aires, where an official welcome ceremony took place in the airport's military area.
Upon the aircraft's arrival, Apostolic Nuncio to Argentina Archbishop Michael Wallace Banach and the Argentinian Chief of Protocol boarded the plane to greet the Pope.
Argentinian President Javier Milei then welcomed Pope Leo XIV at the foot of the aircraft's stairs.
The official ceremony included military honours, the national anthems of the Holy See and Argentina, and a floral offering presented by two children. The respective delegations were also introduced.
Archbishop Banach, who was appointed Apostolic Nuncio to Argentina on 14 May 2026, and Archbishop Marcelo Daniel Colombo of Mendoza, President of the Argentinian Episcopal Conference, are among the Church representatives accompanying the Pope's visit.
The visit carries particular significance given Buenos Aires' close connection with Pope Francis, who served as Archbishop of the Argentine capital from 28 February 1998 until his election as Pope on 13 March 2013.
Buenos Aires, Argentina's capital and most populous city, is situated on the western bank of the Río de la Plata. It is one of the major political, cultural and financial centres of Latin America and has long been a focal point of the country's social and economic life.
Founded in 1536 by Spanish conquistador Pedro de Mendoza and re-established in 1580 by Juan de Garay, the city became the capital of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776. It played a central role in Argentina's struggle for independence, which began with the May Revolution of 1810.
Today, Buenos Aires is divided into 15 communes and 48 neighbourhoods, known as barrios . Its history has also been shaped by successive waves of immigration, particularly from Europe during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
Following the official welcome and meeting with the Argentinian President, Pope Leo XIV is scheduled to travel by car to Plaza San Martín, just over 6 kilometres from the airport.
Located in the Retiro neighbourhood, the historic square is named after General José de San Martín, one of the principal leaders of South America's independence movements and a national hero in Argentina, Chile and Peru.
At its centre stands the equestrian monument dedicated to San Martín and the armies of independence. The square was named in his honour in 1878, on the centenary of his birth, and subsequently developed into one of Buenos Aires' principal public spaces.
The Pope's arrival in Argentina marks the second stage of his 12-day, three-country apostolic journey, which began in Uruguay and will conclude in Peru on 16 November.

articles.title_orig: Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles as Aramco building in Riyadh is damaged, and other Mideast news
articles.title_zh: Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles as Aramco building in Riyadh is damaged, and other Mideast news
articles.content_orig:
The Aramco Tower, a skyscraper in the Saudi Arabian capital's central financial district, had been hit by an air attack.
A statement issued via the Houthi-controlled Saba news agency confirmed the group had targeted Riyadh's business zone on Saturday, without mentioning the Aramco Tower by name.
The Saudi energy ministry said the tower had suffered only "minor damage" and no one had been killed or injured.
Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows more extensive damage to the building, with at least one floor appearing to have been badly hit by a missile or drone strike.
Windows on more than one level appear to have been shattered by the strike.
The Houthis also said Riyadh's airport and Aramco oil storage facilities were targeted in separate strikes. Saudi Arabia said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed several missiles.
The strikes were the latest claimed by the Yemen-based armed group against targets deep inside Saudi Arabia, which the Gulf power has struggled to contain in recent months.
It came a day after the Houthis accused a Saudi-led coalition of killing at least 33 people , including women and children, in an air strike on Yemen.
Footage broadcast by Houthi-run television channel Al Masirah showed rescuers pulling bodies from the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.
Saba said 39 people had been injured in the strike. Saudi Arabia has not commented.
A Saudi-led coalition has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government, which has lost control of a large swathe of the country to the rebel group.
Although the conflict had largely been dormant in recent years, fighting has intensified following the outbreak of the Iran war.
An informal ceasefire unravelled in July after the Tehran-backed Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they have called a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport Saudi Arabia said had been to prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing there.
Major fighting has since resumed between Houthi forces and troops aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.
