articles.title_orig: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.title_zh: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.content_orig:
Bailiffs reportedly seized digital records before court case over alleged intellectual property breaches on Land Rover Defender
Bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover raided the Dutch offices of a Chinese “copycat” rival before a legal showdown this week over whether its “Defender clone” infringes intellectual property rights.
Bailiffs acting on behalf of JLR reportedly seized digital records from the offices of Chinese carmaker BYD in Schiedam and Hoofddorp in August, according to the Sunday Times.
The raid took place before a court case in the The Hague this week which will decide whether the BYD has a case to answer over allegations that its Ti7 SUV infringes the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender.
Motoring experts have likened BYD’s seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV to the Defender since it went on sale in China in September last year. The company is scheduled to launch the vehicle, which the BBC’s Top Gear magazine called the “Chinese Defender clone” , in the UK market in January at a price of £47,995, undercutting the Defender by more than £20,000.
BYD says on its website that “an unapologetically boxy profile delivers the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look”.
The price of JLR’s seven-seat Defender 110 starts from £68,465and is one of the country’s bestselling cars. The UK-based carmaker, which is owned by India’s Tata Motors, sold 29,500 Defenders to retail customers between July and September this year, compared with 25,370a year earlier.
The raid in the Netherlands was carried out by court-ordered bailiffs, with JLR suspecting that BYD reverse-engineered some of the technology that could be used in the Ti7, the Times reported. JLR wanted to secure the digital records before they could be destroyed.
JLR and BYD declined to comment on the “ongoing legal proceedings”.
The dispute with BYD is not the first legal case JLR has pursed against a Chinese company over copycat allegations. It won a legal case to stop Jiangling Motor Corporation selling a copycat vehicle in 2019 after a three-year court battle.
after newsletter promotion
In some cases JLR has taken a collaborative approach to dealing with the rise of China’s carmakers. It agreed to form a joint venture with Chery in a 2012 deal which later included licensing its discontinued Freelander brand with the company.
Chery’s Jaecoo model, which is not part of the joint venture, has been called the Temu Range Rover because of its similarities to the JLR vehicle after years of collaboration between the pair. It costs £10,000 less than JLR’s Range Rover.
The Jaecoo was the bestselling car in the UK in October, with 10,813 registrations, taking its market share from 2.07% to 4.30%, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers & Traders. JLR’s sales of the Range Rover fell to 43,300 in the third quarter of this year, from 47,196 cars sold in the same months last year.

articles.title_orig: Scoop: Trump asked Netanyahu to move on Gaza peace plan in post-election call
articles.title_zh: Scoop: Trump asked Netanyahu to move on Gaza peace plan in post-election call
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a recent phone call to advance his Gaza peace plan, signaling that the administration wants to move forward with the next phase following Israel's election, Axios reported Sunday.
According to two sources familiar with the conversation, Trump wants to advance the roadmap despite uncertainty over who will form Israel's next government.
The plan calls for disarming Hamas, demilitarizing the Gaza Strip, and transferring responsibility for governing the territory to a new Palestinian technocratic government.
The initiative has been stalled for months, largely because of domestic political considerations surrounding Israel's election campaign.
The Trump administration sought to keep the Gaza plan from becoming a contentious issue during the campaign. Trump endorsed Netanyahu shortly before the Oct. 27 election but now wants to proceed regardless of whether Netanyahu or his political opposition forms the next government.
The call marks a renewed push to implement the second phase of Trump's 20-point peace initiative, which began with a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas a year ago. The first phase secured the release of the last 20 living hostages taken during Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attacks on Israel.
Trump's Board of Peace, established as part of the agreement, has spent months developing a framework that includes a Palestinian technocratic administration and an international stabilization force.
In July, the Board of Peace reached an agreement with Hamas on a 15-point proposal to disarm armed groups in Gaza and transfer civilian and security responsibilities to the proposed Palestinian government.
Netanyahu's government has largely resisted advancing the proposal, citing concerns about Hamas' intentions and continued military activity.
During an August visit to Israel, Trump adviser Jared Kushner told Netanyahu that Hamas had agreed for the first time to disarm. Kushner urged the prime minister to take steps to determine whether the group's commitment was genuine.
Netanyahu has remained deeply skeptical, arguing that Hamas is rebuilding its military capabilities and rearming in Gaza.
Over the past three months, the Board of Peace has worked with Israeli government and military officials to refine the proposal and address concerns about how Hamas would be disarmed.
A U.S. official said the plan would proceed gradually, with reconstruction beginning only after verified progress toward disarming Hamas.
In September, the Board of Peace unveiled a six-month, $2.45 billion initial recovery plan for Gaza at the U.N. General Assembly. The proposal includes 66 projects addressing postwar reconstruction and governance.
Moving forward will require cooperation from both Israel and Hamas.
A source familiar with the discussions said the Trump administration, the Board of Peace, and Israel agree that the proposal remains the best available path forward and that there is no credible alternative.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Kushner, and U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff also participated in Thursday's phone call, which Netanyahu initiated.
A source familiar with the conversation described the call as constructive and said the participants also discussed the war in Iran.
Former British Prime Minister Tony Blair, a member of the Board of Peace, visited Israel on Friday and met with Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming a new government.
A source familiar with Blair's visit said the former prime minister urged Netanyahu and other Israeli political leaders to support the Gaza initiative.
"The implementation will be difficult but we believe it is a good plan for Israel. Nevertheless we can't do it with one hand tied behind our back," the U.S. official said.
"We want to move forward collaboratively and we need full cooperation and partnership from the Israeli government," the official added.

articles.content_orig:
More than 200,000 people have taken to the streets of Amsterdam in the Netherlands, demanding government action against Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, according to the Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organisers.
Sunday’s ‘Red Line’ protesters, many wearing red items of clothing, called for tighter trade restrictions on Israel and a halt to all arms sales.
“What is happening there is inhumane,” Mike van Dongen said as he walked in the huge throng of people.
“As far as I’m concerned, [the Dutch authorities] are doing nothing,” he said. “They don’t dare take any serious steps.”
As the protesters marched along a normally busy Amsterdam street that was closed to traffic on Sunday, a man stood at a bus stop with a loudspeaker shouting, “Free, free Palestine!” Many of the marchers echoed his cry as they passed.
Israel’s genocidal war has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians, including 21,000 children, since October 2023.
Sunday’s protest was similar to one in early October last year. That followed ‘Red Line’ demonstrations last June when protesters marched through the streets of The Hague.
A “ ceasefire ” took effect in Gaza on October 10 last year, but Israeli attacks and killings have continued on an almost-daily basis since.
The war in Gaza has strained relations between the Netherlands and Israel. The Dutch foreign minister resigned last year after failing to secure new sanctions against Israel.
Since then, a new minority coalition government took power in February and introduced an import ban on products from Israeli settlements, which the Dutch government and most of the international community consider illegal – the ban provoked a diplomatic spat with Israel.
Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who took part in a march last year but was not present on Sunday, defended his government’s actions at his weekly news conference on Friday.
“Every single day and every single week, we do what we can to alleviate the terrible situation there,” he said.
He added that his administration is “exerting greater political and diplomatic pressure” on Israel to abide by its agreements on Gaza.

articles.title_orig: 3 Affordable Retro Consoles You Can Buy From GameStop
articles.title_zh: 3 Affordable Retro Consoles You Can Buy From GameStop
articles.content_orig:
There is no doubt: retro gaming is on the rise, partly because modern electronics are getting more expensive and partly because it's growing in popularity among collectors. While we can mitigate the effects of RAM and storage shortages by leaning on retro gaming to avoid the high costs of current-generation gaming consoles, the impact of collectors is harder to ignore. The good news is that plenty of flash carts can lower the overall cost of retro gaming, letting gamers focus their budget on the consoles themselves. That is, if you haven't already built a retro gaming setup using hardware you already own .
Thankfully, GameStop has taken it upon itself to flesh out its retro selection for the modern day. This means it sells a wide selection of older consoles and games at affordable prices, which is precisely what this article is about: affordable retro consoles you can buy from GameStop. We've chosen three consoles that each fall under $200: the PS1, the GBA for some handheld goodness, and the somewhat more niche Dreamcast to round out the selection.
Of course, these are all older systems, which means their condition will depend on the item you buy, so like all used goods, make sure to research and compare a few units to ensure you get one that looks and plays well. GameStop at least tests all units to ensure they work, with a pre-owned guarantee that includes a seven-day money-back window, but appearances can vary, so keep a close eye on it while you shop.
If you're looking for a large library of retro games, the PS1 is a great starting point. After all, the console sold over 102 million units, so there's a library of 4,000+ titles. While many were never released in English, the good news is that plenty of English hacks are available for games never released in this region. This is where soft modding a PS1 comes in, which requires loading a PS memory card with custom software like FreePSXBoot.
GameStop tends to list the PS1 and PS1 Slim for around $70, which is highly affordable, though game prices can differ depending on whether it's a complete game in the box with the manual, or just the disc. But even the more coveted titles like Vagrant Story (~$50) and Suikoden II (~$100) aren't that bad compared to platforms where classics can sell for $300 or more a pop. When it comes to retro gaming, prices are relative, but thankfully the PS1 hasn't yet been mined for all its worth like some other retro systems (looking at you, Neo Geo Pocket), likely because there are so many PS1 games and consoles still out there.
In other words, the PS1 is a fine retro gaming starting point for anyone who doesn't want to spend a fortune before they boot a title. One can scratch their nostalgia itch with some classics, and once you grow bored, there's a wealth of game hacks to explore, from fan translations to backports of non-PS1 games. It's easy to keep busy with a retro PS1 at home, all without breaking the bank.
The Nintendo Game Boy Advance SP is a retro console that can play just about every title in the Game Boy line, from GB to GBC to GBA. This adds up to 3,000+ games across all three. The only caveat is that the first SP (AGS-001) used front lighting, which can wash out a game's colors. Later models (AGS-101) switched to proper backlighting, with two brightness levels to choose from. GameStop doesn't specify which model you'll receive when ordering online, so you may want to head to a brick-and-mortar store, especially since GBA SP models sell for $160, right on the edge of affordable.
The console is only part of the expense, and some Game Boy titles can get pricey; make sure to investigate the cost of each title. The good news is that there are plenty of affordable flash carts on the market, from single ROM carts to ones that can house the entire library with a microSD, gadgets that make retro gaming feel modern . Flash carts also make it easy to play hacks; there are a slew of colorized ROMs from the original GB, plus tons of translations that allow fans to explore classics that never came to the States.
Yes, a Game Boy Advance SP is more of an investment than a PS1, but you get portability with your purchase while gaining access to a similarly sized library. The games are also much smaller than discs and easier to store, which may be important if you plan to collect. By and large, if you're interested in the world of retro gaming, a Game Boy Advance SP offers plenty of benefits that make it a great place to start your journey without straining your wallet too hard.
If you'd like to explore a smaller, more niche retro platform, the Sega Dreamcast offers a library of 600+ games. Many of these are absolute gems, like Shenmue, Jet Grind Radio, and Phantasy Star Online. A Dreamcast and controller tend to go for $160 at GameStop, and there are plenty of reasons why retro game enthusiasts love old controllers like the Dreamcast's. However, this price doesn't include the Visual Memory Unit (a memory card), which retails for around $25. Be sure to factor in both items, plus the games you want. Titles like Crazy Taxi can be found for $20, but more collectible games like Jet Grind Radio often cost $50.
The Sega Dreamcast has a thriving modding community, with new games released for the platform, plus fan mods and translations. The Dreamcast can run custom software; you just need a console that supports MIL-CD, and many do. The underside of the machine will reveal a circled zero or one, both of which indicate MIL-CD support, allowing you to play software burned to a CD-R. However, a machine with a circled two may not support MIL-CD, so head to a brick-and-mortar store where you can inspect the console.
Ultimately, if you're interested in a much more focused retro experience, one where you won't get lost in the weeds of a giant library, the Dreamcast delivers a variety of quality games that are still affordable. And if you pick up the right hardware, you can easily play the majority on the cheap by spinning up a CD-R drive, leaving yourself room to purchase the occasional original on disc the next time you visit GameStop.

articles.title_orig: Egypt train crash: At least seven killed and dozens injured
articles.title_zh: Egypt train crash: At least seven killed and dozens injured
articles.content_orig:
This live page has now closed - read more in our news story
At least seven people have died and dozens are injured after a train collision in al-Ayyat in Egypt's Giza governorate, the local health ministry says
A train driver is among those killed , the ministry adds - it's not yet clear what caused the collision
More than 70 ambulances have been deployed to the scene, officials say, with at least 112 people thought to have sustained injuries
Three hospitals are being used to treat the wounded, the health ministry says in its statement
Images show derailed train carriages with large crowds of people nearby, and Egyptian Red Crescent workers at the scene
This crash site has a long history of rail disasters, writes our reporter , including the country's deadliest when hundreds of people died in 2002 after a passenger train was engulfed in flames
At least seven people - including a driver - have been killed in a train collision in Egypt.
The country's health ministry says that 112 others have been injured and are being treated at three different hospitals near the crash site in al-Ayyat, south of Giza.
More than 70 ambulances were scrambled to the scene - authorities say the final number of fatalities is still being counted.
A train heading from Giza to Fayoum - south of Cairo - collided into the back of a service heading from Cairo to Aswan in the south, which is believed to have been stationary, according to Egypt's Public Prosecution Office.
The cause of the crash is yet to be officially determined and prosecutors have launched an investigation. Our reporter writes the site of the collision has a long history of rail disasters.
Images and footage from the scene show several derailed passenger carriages overturned along the tracks - you can watch that below.
We're now ending our live coverage, you can keep up to date in our news story.
Samantha Granville Middle East reporter
As well as this latest train collision, deadly rail disasters have also struck elsewhere in the country.
In August 2017, two passenger trains collided near the Mediterranean city of Alexandria, killing more than 40 people and injuring dozens.
Egypt was the first country in Africa and the Middle East to introduce railways. Today, around 110 million people rely on the network.
But while billions have been invested in roads and high-speed rail projects, much of the country's ageing railway infrastructure is still in need of modernisation.
Foreign leaders are expressing condolences and support for the victims of today's train collision in al-Ayyat, 73km (45 miles) south of Giza.
Saudi Arabia's ministry of foreign affairs expressed "solidarity" with Egypt and wished the injured a speedy recovery.
The Turkish ambassador to Egypt wrote on X that he extended "heartfelt condolences and sincere sympathy" to the victims, their families and the Egyptian people.
Yemen's foreign ministry extends its condolences to those affected by the deadly train crash and Jordan's foreign ministry echoes the sentiment sharing its condolences.
Wael Hussein BBC News, reporting from Cairo
The two trains involved in Sunday's collision serve very different journeys â but both are important transport links for ordinary Egyptians.
The first was travelling to Fayoum, around 100km (62 miles) from Cairo, while the second was heading south to Aswan, nearly 900km (559 miles) away.
Both services are used largely by lower-income passengers, for whom train travel is one of the most affordable ways to get around the country. Tickets for the shorter journey cost less than $1, while the longer trip to Aswan costs less than $10.
Getting eyewitness accounts and personal testimonies can take time.
Many passengers on these services come from poorer communities and may not own smartphones, meaning photographs, videos and first-hand accounts of what happened can take longer to emerge.
More now from the Public Prosecution Office statement.
The office says that after an inspection of the scene, and speaking to eyewitnesses, they have determined that the front of the train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the back of the Cairo-Aswan rail service.
It adds that the train in front (Cairo-Aswan service) had stopped on the tracks. Both trains were heading in the same direction, the statement says.
On the number of deaths, the office says the final number of fatalities and injuries is still being counted but initial estimates say seven people, including the driver of the Giza to Fayoum train, died and 114 have been injured.
This figure differs slightly from the latest update from the country's health ministry, who say 112 people have been injured.
Egypt's public prosecutors have launched a formal investigation into the train collision that has killed at least seven people.
In a statement on Facebook, the Public Prosecution Office says it will work to determine the circumstances that caused the crash.
Investigators will examine the damaged carriages, tracks, surrounding area and work to identify any "shortcomings" in operational procedures and safety measures, the statement adds.
Youssef Taha BBC World Service News
Heavy machinery has been dispatched to the crash site to remove the overturned carriages
It's still unclear what caused the accident.
Heavy lifting equipment is at the scene and Transport Minister Kamel al-Wazir is visiting the site.
There have been calls for him to resign such is the frequency of fatal train crashes in Egypt.
President Abdel-Fattah al-Sisi has ordered an urgent investigation saying that those responsible will be held accountable.
Samantha Granville Middle East reporter
More than 300 people were killed in a fire on a train travelling through the Giza governorate in 2002
The site of Sunday's accident in al-Ayyat, in Egypt's Giza governorate, has a long history of rail disasters.
It was the location of Egypt's deadliest train tragedy.
In February 2002, a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor.
The train continued for around nine kilometres before coming to a halt. More than 370 people were officially reported killed, although some estimates put the toll considerably higher.
Two further crashes in the area in 2009 killed dozens more.
More now from the health ministry's latest statement.
Egypt's Health Minister Dr. Khaled Abdel Ghaffar continues to monitor the consequences of the train derailment, the statement says.
It adds that he has ordered all health facilities in the Giza and Beni Suef governorates to raise their level of preparedness and provide all necessary medical and emergency support to the injured.
Injuries sustained in the crash include bruising, fractured limbs, pelvis, and vertebrae and cuts to the head and face, the statement says.
"The remaining injured are continuing treatment under medical observation."
The number of people who have died following the train collision has risen to seven, with 112 others injured, according to the Egyptian health ministry.
It adds that 45 people who had been sent to hospital have now been discharged.
Earlier, the ministry reported four people - including a train driver - had been killed and 88 injured.
The Egyptian Red Crescent is at the scene of the crash, helping victims and their families.
The organisation says on its Facebook page that it dispatched teams from its headquarters, and branches in Giza, Fayoum and Beni Suef, to provide assistance and psychological support.
"The Egyptian Red Crescent, along with all its staff and volunteers, extends its deepest condolences and sympathy to the families of the victims," the post adds.
At least four people have been killed and dozens injured in a passenger train collision in Egypt, the country's health ministry says.
We don't know: what caused the crash, the identities of the other fatalities, the conditions of those in hospital or if there are still people in the carriages.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang reportedly targeted by Beijing-recruited spy
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang reportedly targeted by Beijing-recruited spy
articles.content_orig:
Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle are ramping up calls for investigations into reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Some are also questioning what the Trump administration knew about the matter.
"The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires, the more I'm convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn't corrupt," Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., posted on X on Saturday. "Congress will investigate and get answers."
Coons is in line to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when his party takes control of the chamber in January.
Three House Republican committee chairs sent a letter to Huang on Wednesday requesting that he sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18, a day after the company is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People's Republic of China's] access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the GOP lawmakers wrote in a letter to Huang .
The reports refer to Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company that the U.S. has suspected of helping China circumvent artificial intelligence chip sales prohibitions.
Policymakers in the Trump administration received a memo last spring with intelligence identifying Alice Huang as having been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security and revealing her relationship with Nvidia's chief executive, The New York Times first reported on Friday.
When asked by the Times whether Huang would appear before lawmakers to discuss the matter, Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo declined to comment. "Our chief executive has an outstanding security team that accompanies him where needed," Mr. Rizzo said in a statement to the Times.
Rizzo said the Nvidia CEO's interactions with Ms. Huang were consistent with meetings he has had with any of Nvidia's customers, the Times reported .
Separately, Texas Republican Sen. John Cornyn shared a Times article published Saturday reporting that the Trump administration approved a Chinese firm, New Matrix, to assemble chips for Nvidia in Beijing. The Times found little evidence of meaningful operations at its listed address, despite Trump's Commerce Department clearing it for national security risks.
Cornyn called the report "outrageous" in his post on X .
Rep. Seth Magaziner, D-R.I., who sits on the House Committee on Homeland Security, called on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify before Congress along with Huang.
Neither Nvidia nor the Commerce Department immediately responded to CNBC's request for comment.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot tapped to form Israeli government
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot tapped to form Israeli government
articles.content_orig:
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar ("Straight") party, waves an Israeli flag onstage last month in Tel Aviv following the release of the first exit poll results in Israel's general election. Ariel Schalit/AP hide caption
Israel's president has tapped Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, to try to form the next government. It's a setback for Netanyahu, whose party won the most seats but failed to secure a parliamentary majority.
Netanyahu's Likud party won 27 seats in last month's election, six more than Eisenkot's Yashar party. But neither secured enough support to command a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament.
President Isaac Herzog will formally give Eisenkot the mandate at 5 p.m. local time on Sunday. Herzog made the decision after parties representing most of the members of Israel's parliament recommended Eisenkot to try forming a governing coalition.
Eisenkot is a former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces, serving as the country's top military commander from 2015 to 2019. A veteran of several military campaigns, he later joined Netanyahu's emergency war cabinet following the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks on Israel, but left the following year, accusing Netanyahu of failing to make progress toward ending the Gaza war and securing the release of hostages.
Eisenkot lost his son, Gal, a reservist killed in Gaza, as well as two nephews during the war.
He leads the center-right Yashar party, which he founded on an anti-corruption and government reform platform. He will now have 28 days to put together a coalition government, with a possible 14-day extension.
That gives him up to six weeks to negotiate with rival parties and secure the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority.
The coalition building promises to be a tough task and could include strange bedfellows: from ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties to Arab-led parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel — who make up about 20% of Israel and had a record turnout in these elections.
They could now potentially be the kingmakers. But both Eisenkot and Netanyahu ruled out working with them before the elections. Now there's some public pressure on Eisenkot to change his mind, and on Saturday Netanyahu issued a video warning against that.
He said it would be partnering with what he called Hamas supporters and "those who oppose Judaism." Eisenkot responded, calling Netanyahu's video hysterical.
If Eisenkot fails, Herzog can give another lawmaker a chance to form a government. If those efforts also fail, Israel could face another election. Netanyahu would remain caretaker prime minister in the meantime.

Country music star Terri Clark tells OutKick OutDoors how fishing helps her unwind, shares her favorite moments on the water and laughs about practicing fishing knots on her tour bus.
Deer facing off with one another and settling matters physically isn't reserved for just the bucks during rutting season. Female deer will throw down too, especially if they feel the need to protect their young.
Back in September, this was on display in an amateur photographer's backyard. She heard noises coming from the yard and when she looked out of her window she saw two does going at it.

articles.title_orig: Rosstat hack: data obtained suggests over 390,000 Russian deaths in Ukraine war
articles.title_zh: Rosstat hack: data obtained suggests over 390,000 Russian deaths in Ukraine war
articles.content_orig:
The hacker groups Kiberpartizany BY and Silent Crow claim to have carried out a large-scale breach of Russia's Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat).
According to the hackers, they managed to steal about 23 terabytes of data, including internal documents, demographic and economic statistics, as well as information on Russian losses in the war against Ukraine.
The data obtained enabled the groups to make their own calculations of the number of people killed since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
According to Kiberpartizany BY, as of 27 August 2026 at least 393,881 Russian citizens have been killed in the war. Silent Crow gives an even higher figure of 450,100 dead.
This significant difference in estimates is due to the use of different methods of counting losses.
Kiberpartizany BY counted deaths in which military action or its consequences were listed as the cause.
Silent Crow, by contrast, not only included those killed in combat, but also added several other categories of deaths: non-combat losses among military personnel, deaths marked as terrorist acts, and deaths of people registered in Russia but who died in occupied territories or in Ukraine where the exact cause of death was not established.
Russia has not released official statistics on combat losses since September 2022.
In addition, from 2024 Rosstat stopped publishing annual data on causes of death, which has made an independent assessment of the demographic impact of the war much more difficult.
Against this backdrop, access to the agency's internal statistical materials may make it possible to assess the scale of human losses more accurately.
For comparison, as of 8 November the joint database of BBC News Russian Service and Mediazona, which collects a list of dead Russian servicemen identified by name, contained around 286,000 names. However, this list is known to be incomplete, especially for the most recent months of the war.
In a joint study by Meduza and Mediazona, based on analysis of inheritance registry data, the number of fallen Russian servicemen by the end of 2025 was estimated at roughly 350,000.
In this way, the hackers' estimates are in line with figures from previously published independent studies, although this does not yet prove the accuracy of each individual number.
Meduza and Mediazona have said they obtained access to the data published by the hackers and have begun checking it.
The journalists aim to establish not only whether the materials are authentic, but also how complete the information is they contain. In particular, they need to rule out the possibility of deliberate data falsification.
Moreover, causes of death given in medical documents do not always reflect the actual circumstances of a person's death.
It should also be noted that Rosstat's internal databases do not contain up-to-date information on people listed as missing. Such individuals may be declared dead only after a long period of time.
Therefore even data from the state statistics agency cannot automatically provide a definitive figure for Russian military losses.
If the authenticity and completeness of the leak are confirmed, the materials obtained could become one of the largest sources of information on the demographic consequences of the war for Russia.

articles.title_orig: South Africa’s ANC is humbled by its worst election results
articles.title_zh: South Africa’s ANC is humbled by its worst election results
articles.content_orig:
South Africa's municipal election is unlikely to produce an immediate shift in the country's policy toward Israel, but the African National Congress's (ANC) declining electoral dominance could make it increasingly difficult for the party to maintain its diplomatic position without facing challenges from its coalition partners, Jason Halfon told The Jerusalem Post .
Halfon is a South African based in Israel who previously held leadership positions in the Democratic Alliance party and is a graduate of its Young Leaders and, more recently, Catalyst programs.
The November 4 local elections saw the ANC suffer significant losses, with its share of the national proportional representation vote falling to approximately 30.9%, down from 45.6% in 2021. The Democratic Alliance (DA) received approximately 24.7%, up from 21.7%, while the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party received approximately 9.8%.
Halfon argued that the results should not be viewed solely in the context of the ANC's declining popularity, but also as evidence of the growing fragmentation of political power in South Africa.
Seven of South Africa's eight metropolitan municipalities are heading toward coalition negotiations, with no party securing an outright majority.
Although the election does not directly affect the composition of South Africa's national government, the results could have implications for the balance of power within the governing coalition, particularly as parties prepare for the next national elections.
Halfon told the Post that the losses also carry organizational consequences for the ANC itself. Municipal control has long functioned as a key source of party revenue through contributions from public representatives and as a vehicle for local patronage networks. Losing council seats and executive positions reduces both income streams and the party’s ability to direct appointments and procurement, he opined.
Halfon noted that the full impact of these losses is likely to become clearer in the period leading up to the ANC’s 2027 elective conference, when internal mobilization and branch-level resources become decisive.
Municipal councils do not determine South Africa's diplomatic policy, as the Presidency, the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO), and the national executive remain the principal centers of foreign-policy decision-making.
Nevertheless, the results could strengthen the political standing of parties seeking to challenge ANC policies, particularly the DA, which participates in the national Government of National Unity (GNU).
Halfon said the DA remains the largest non-ANC party in the GNU and is essential to its parliamentary majority. While alternative partners exist on paper, any sustained turn toward parties that themselves emerged from ANC fractures would risk accelerating further splits.
This structural position, he argued, creates "latent leverage" that could be exercised through contestation of key appointments, demands for formal coordination on major foreign-policy decisions, and the linking of municipal coalition negotiations to broader governance issues.
For Israel, the question is whether this redistribution of political power could eventually translate into a more pragmatic South African foreign policy.
Halfon thinks it could, but "indirectly, and only over time."
While foreign policy is not decided in municipal chambers, the "diffusion of power across major councils changes the internal balance inside the GNU," he explained.
"Single-party dominance of diplomatic posture becomes harder to maintain when coalition partners control significant local executive authority and can link national cooperation to broader governance demands."
While Halfon said a shift would not produce sudden alignment with Israel, he suggested that the results could eventually encourage a "gradual move toward greater pragmatism." This could mean prioritizing economic and technological interests such as water management, agriculture, and municipal innovation in South Africa's relationship with Israel, rather than allowing ideological considerations to dominate diplomatic decision-making.
Halfon noted that South Africa’s large Christian population also gives practical weight to the cost of restricted travel and pilgrimage links.
"These factors create space for recalibration if non-ANC parties consistently use their municipal and national leverage to demand it," he noted.
The ANC has historically made support for the Palestinian cause a central part of its foreign policy and political identity.
This position has become particularly well-known since December 2023, when South Africa brought a case against Israel before the International Court of Justice (ICJ), accusing it of violating the Genocide Convention through its military activity in Gaza. Israel has rejected the allegations and challenged the court's jurisdiction.
The case remains ongoing, with the ICJ setting November 22, 2027, as the deadline for South Africa's next written submission and May 22, 2029, for Israel's response. The court has not issued a final ruling on the genocide allegations.
Halfon said the ANC's support for the Palestinian cause remains "institutionally entrenched," even though the original framework that once contained it has largely eroded.
"Historically the ANC maintained a more complex position," he told the Post . "A disproportionate number of South African Jews, drawing on their own experience of persecution, played significant roles in the anti-apartheid struggle. Nelson Mandela explicitly recognized the legitimacy of Zionism as Jewish national self-determination while simultaneously supporting Palestinian aspirations. He saw no necessary contradiction."
According to Halfon, that balance began to narrow as the ANC transitioned from a liberation movement into South Africa's governing party.
"Today the position functions less as a carefully weighed principle and more as a source of elite cohesion, international signaling, and domestic distraction," he continued.
The ANC's claim of historical solidarity with liberation movements "has become harder to sustain on two practical grounds," Halfon added.
"First, consistency: Equivalent diplomatic energy and legal activism are not applied to other severe human-rights crises, including the mass internment of Uyghurs or the large-scale killing of Christians in parts of Africa. Selective application weakens the claim that the policy is driven by universal principle."
"Second, opportunity cost. South Africa faces collapsing municipal infrastructure, unreliable water and power, and high levels of violence. The expenditure of diplomatic capital and state resources on a distant conflict while basic services deteriorate is increasingly difficult to justify to voters who judge parties on local outcomes."
Halfon argued that, although support for the Palestinian cause remains deeply embedded within the ANC, "its political returns are diminishing relative to its costs."
The municipal election results could reinforce that pressure by demonstrating that voters want more focus on domestic governance issues, particularly infrastructure, service delivery and public safety. However, they do not necessarily indicate that voters are rejecting the ANC's position on Israel.
For Israel and South Africa's Jewish community, Halfon said the results should primarily be seen as evidence that South African voters are judging parties on local delivery and accountability rather than international signaling.
"For Israel and the local Jewish community, the practical implication is straightforward," he said. "The era of unchallenged single-party control of diplomatic posture is ending. The quality of the coalitions that emerge, and the willingness of non-ANC parties to treat foreign policy as a legitimate area of negotiation rather than a reserved domain, will determine whether that change produces a more balanced and interest-driven approach."

articles.title_orig: Motorola is quietly building apps and features that make Pixel and Samsung phones feel behind the times
articles.title_zh: Motorola is quietly building apps and features that make Pixel and Samsung phones feel behind the times
articles.content_orig:
I haven't thought much about Motorola since I dropped my Razr V3 several years back. After Android took over, a Google Pixel or a Samsung was always the easy pick for me.
That changed when I went through the spec sheet for Motorola's Signature flagship . The Signature 27 is due in November 2026 with features I didn't know I wanted.
So I dug through Motorola's announcement to see what it's promising and where Google and Samsung have an answer.
Google built its Tensor chips around on-device AI features and accepted slower raw performance to get there. The Signature 27 doesn't make the same trade.
Motorola uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, one of two 2nm chips Qualcomm announced at Snapdragon Summit in September 2026. Its two fastest cores run at up to 5.01GHz, while the Tensor G6 in the Pixel 11 Pro tops out at 4.11GHz.
Qualcomm says the Extreme chip has 13% faster CPU performance and a 44% faster GPU than the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. That's the chip in the Galaxy S26 Ultra, which means Samsung's best phone uses an older chip until the next Galaxy launches.
Motorola also fitted six antennas, which it says double download speeds and help with cloud AI features.
The chip also helps with privacy, since its security features are a big reason GrapheneOS picked the Signature 27 as its first non-Pixel phone . Until now, GrapheneOS only officially supported Pixels.
Seven years of OS upgrades only keep Motorola level with Google and Samsung, which promise the same. What makes the promise believable this time is how early Motorola moved on Android 17.
It opened an Android 17 beta in February 2026 and started the stable rollout in August with the original Signature.
More than 50 Motorola phones are on the list, which is a big change for a brand I remember as slow with updates. It's the first Motorola flagship I'd expect to last as long as my Pixel.
A fast chip only stays fast while it's cool, because phone chips throttle when heat builds up. Most mainstream flagships handle this with a vapor chamber and stop there.
Gaming phones go further, and the Infinix GT 50 Pro even runs a liquid-cooling loop . The Signature 27 takes a middle route between the two.
Motorola's ArcticMesh system stacks diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal, and copper mesh with a redesigned 3D vapor chamber. Motorola says that the vapor chamber is 40% larger than the one in the original Signature.
It aims to maintain steady performance during gaming, AI tasks, and long video recordings. I'm still cautious, though, because a phone this thin can only dissipate so much heat.
Samsung puts a 200MP sensor on the Galaxy S26 Ultra's main camera. Motorola puts its 200MP sensor on the periscope telephoto, next to a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera.
Vivo and Xiaomi have shipped 200MP periscopes since 2024, so this isn't new to Android. However, Google and Samsung don't offer it on their flagships right now.
Super Zoom Pro pushes the range to 100x with generative AI. The Pixel 11 Pro reaches 120x, but its telephoto is 48MP, so it has fewer pixels to crop before AI fills in detail.
Motorola's zoom history makes me skeptical, so I want to see 30x samples before I give the 200MP sensor credit.
I'm more interested in video, since that's where Pixel has built its reputation. Motorola's Video Enhancement Engine analyzes the scene before and during recording, then adjusts color tones in real time.
Motorola pairs it with 3.5-degree OIS hardware and Qualcomm's image stabilization to keep handheld footage steady.
Pixel's Video Boost does its processing after you stop recording. Google processes the clip after it backs up to Google Photos, so you need an internet connection, and boosted recordings stop at 10 minutes.
If Motorola's real-time processing gets close to Video Boost quality, I'd take it over waiting on an upload after every concert.
Qira is Lenovo and Motorola's personal AI. It replaces Moto AI on supported phones with Android 17.
With your permission, it connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, and Outlook, and it can complete supported tasks for you. Its Catch Me Up feature gathers missed emails, chat updates, and calendar changes into one summary.
Lenovo says Qira runs on the device where it can, and it encrypts the personal information it stores locally.
Qira isn't exclusive to the Signature 27. Motorola's Android 17 rollout brings it to select Edge, Signature, and Razr phones, plus Lenovo PCs with 16GB of memory and the Moto Watch Ultra.
Qira's limit is that the full experience depends on owning Motorola or Lenovo hardware. The Signature 27 also ships with Gemini, so Qira has to do something Google's assistant can't on the same phone.
Qira also works alongside Smart Connect, Motorola's app for linking your phone to a PC, tablet, TV, or monitor. It handles file sharing and screen mirroring, and it connects to Windows 10 and 11 through a PC app.
Samsung and Pixel do something similar with Link to Windows. But, between Qira and Smart Connect, Motorola is building its own ecosystem on top of Android instead of leaving it all to Google.
None of this makes a Pixel or Galaxy obsolete, and plenty of Pixel owners won't switch even for GrapheneOS .
Still, a 2nm Snapdragon, a 200MP periscope, and real-time video tuning put pressure on Google and Samsung in areas they usually win.
Qira piques my interest the most, because a cross-device assistant that works well could push both companies to improve their own.
Motorola hasn't shared a US price, so I'll wait for the November reviews before deciding whether my next phone has a Motorola logo.

articles.title_orig: 2 big AI narratives wrestle with each other: What to watch this week
articles.title_zh: 2 big AI narratives wrestle with each other: What to watch this week
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Even before the sell-off last week, we've all had the feeling of white-knuckling through the fourth quarter.
Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) IPO prospectus. Big Tech earnings. Bond yields through the roof. An unexpectedly tall blue wave that lifted the stock market up — and threw it back down.
With volatility ( ^VIX ) running hot, investors are balancing on a knife's edge between a flywheel of angst — or a bounce.
As Goldman Sachs' panic gauge suggested, the extremeness may signal more of Friday's bounce to come.
It's a new week, and we'll have plenty of scheduled plot points to guide us.
Of particular note, we're looking forward to CoreWeave ( CRWV ) quarterly results on Tuesday and Nebius Group ( NBIS ) and Cerebras Systems ( CBRS ) on Thursday, a few companies caught up in the data center destruction post-election.
What they have to say about their plans and outlook, the debt markets they've been tapping, and the health of their business will be at the top of mind.
Good timing to have that a mere week after midterms.
On the economic calendar, we're in inflation mode once again, especially after that hot jobs report.
We'll kick off the week with the New York Fed's consumer inflation expectations before getting some actual data on Tuesday — and wholesale inflation figures on Friday to close the week.
What's more important: the chip and AI infrastructure trade or the companies that actually provide AI?
As we wrote in the Morning Brief on Friday, "A data center slowdown is bad for the stock market's AI engine," and "A data center slowdown is good for Big Tech's profit machine."
Can Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Amazon ( AMZN ) deliver AI at least some productivity and tools to clients with the compute they have — and make a lot of money doing so, flipping the switch from growth and scale to monetization?
Maybe! Those companies are healthily in the green since the election, doing just fine amid the broader sell-off. And while Tesla ( TSLA ) has sold off, SpaceX ( SPCX ) is mostly doing fine.
As DataTrek's Nicholas Colas wrote on Thursday, you need to look at the entire week, not just the bloody Thursday, to see the bigger picture (small as that is). And it's pretty clear that this may be reflected in the broad indexes, but it's mostly about chips.
"As for what the market is 'saying' over the last 2 days, we believe the moves are AI-centric, not augurs of a looming recession," Colas wrote, also noting that Google and Co. are doing fine.
The push-pull of the chip narrative and the hyperscaler narrative is the pulse our fingers are on right now.
Friday's blowout jobs report of 165,000 jobs delivered an unexpected verdict about the current state of the labor market: It's better than fine.
Even September's underwhelming 29,000 jobs were adjusted upward to 60,000.
Good for breaking the "low-fire, low-hire" ice, if this represents the beginning of a trend. As every Fed chair likes to remind us, one month doesn't mean anything by itself.
The big takeaway from the report, however, isn't that the labor market is heating up, but that any weakness or recession is not currently something to worry about .
But with Tuesday and Friday's big inflation reports for October, we'll have more than just one data point to work with, and two (or more) hot pieces of economic data could start to make some people sweat.
We are keeping one research note from Apollo's Torsten Sløk that caught our attention last week at the top of our mind: that the Fed's rates needed to bring inflation down its 2% target could be as high as 6.75%. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)
While the data center sell-off is obviously important, inflation still matters as much as anything.
Bloomberg's average analyst estimate has core inflation rising 0.2%, slowing down from 0.3% last month.
Amid all the data will be a lot of commentary from the people who read the data — and decide what to do with it.
The Fed's Goolsbee and Bowman speak on Monday; Waller and Bowman (again) on Tuesday; Barr, Barkin, and Logan on Thursday; and Williams, Jefferson, and Bowman (again) on Friday.
We love seeing our public officials putting in the work. But the market loves guidance and FedSpeak even more and is hoping to be given more of a lens through which to read all of this data and get a better picture of how the Fed sees the economy — and perhaps even the sell-off, depending on what topics come up and how forthcoming they feel like being.
Right now, after Friday's jobs report, the December hike is feeling more likely.
With Fed Chair Warsh settling into a cryptic, taciturn no-forward-guidance rhythm, it's up to these guys — who may also feel more emboldened post-midterms.
As JPMorgan noted last week , the new Democratic Senate leadership is going to be important for the Fed.

articles.title_orig: 5 Things You Need To Do Before You Install Grand Theft Auto 6
articles.title_zh: 5 Things You Need To Do Before You Install Grand Theft Auto 6
articles.content_orig:
One of the most anticipated games of the year is finally almost upon us. "Grand Theft Auto 6" is set to release on November 19, 2026, but preloads will finally unlock on November 10, giving PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S owners a chance to prepare for the game's full release. Many of us have been waiting years to dig into Rockstar Games' latest title, but before you do, it's best to make sure your console is ready for the inevitable hours of playtime you're about to log on it.
If you're planning on preloading the day that the game unlocks, then you'll want to make sure you're ready to go. There are a few things you can do to prepare for the game's release, starting with making sure your console has enough free storage space to hold the download. This is especially important right now, as "GTA 6" won't offer a physical disc edition at all.
The first thing you'll want to look at is how much storage you have left on your console. Rockstar has confirmed that the preload for "GTA 6" will require up to 212 GB of storage space, with the exact size depending on which console you're downloading it on. If you don't have that much free space right now, you'll either have to delete some games or add more storage to your console.
Adding storage only works if it's the right kind, though, because a USB drive won't work for "GTA 6." PS5 games stored on USB extended storage have to be copied back to the console before they can be played, so on PS5, the only real option is an M.2 SSD. On Xbox Series X|S, games have to run from the internal SSD or a Storage Expansion Card. If you'd rather just clear things out instead, there are a few ways to easily free up space on your PlayStation 5 , and Xbox owners can use the console's aptly named Free up space tool to find old add-ons and duplicate files they don't need anymore.
Rockstar says PlayStation 5 owners will be able to start their preload at midnight local time on November 10. Xbox players, on the other hand, will all get access at the same time, as the preload will unlock globally at midnight GMT, which is 7 p.m. ET (4 p.m. PT) on November 9 for players in the United States. That means Xbox players in the U.S. can actually start their download the night before anyone on PS5.
If you're planning to buy a physical copy of the game, it's best to keep in mind that "GTA 6" won't be released on disc . Instead, you'll be given a code within the box that will unlock the digital version of the game. It's also worth noting that physical copies aren't expected to reach retailers until November 12. So be prepared to wait a few more days before you can preload the game. PlayStation codes are also region locked, and the Ultimate Edition won't be available in stores. Instead, you'll need to buy that upgrade after redeeming your code.
One reason you'll want to start preloading as soon as possible is because of how big "Grand Theft Auto 6" is. The game is roughly 212 GB, and depending on your internet speeds, it might take a while to download.
You'll also want to install any system updates before the preload goes live. On Xbox, the console checks for updates every night by default, but if a mandatory update is waiting to be installed, you won't be able to connect to Xbox network services until you install it. If your console hasn't been turned on in a while, it's best to turn it on and check for updates before the preload unlocks, so you don't have to wait on an update before you can start downloading "GTA 6." PS5 owners can skip some of that, since system updates can download and install on their own in Rest Mode as long as the console is set to stay connected to the internet.
Not everyone is going to be able to stay up until midnight to start the preload, and thankfully you don't have to. Both consoles can download "GTA 6" on their own, but you'll need to make sure a couple of settings are turned on first. Rockstar's preload FAQ says that on PS5, you'll need automatic downloads turned on, and the console has to be either powered on or in Rest Mode. In addition to that, you'll want to make sure that Stay Connected to the Internet is turned on in the PS5's Rest Mode settings, as the console won't be able to download anything while it's in Rest Mode without it.
Xbox players will need to turn on automatic updates and leave the console either on or in Sleep mode. If your Xbox is currently set to the energy-saving Shutdown mode, it won't be able to download the preload while it's turned off. Microsoft changed the default power settings for Xbox consoles in 2023, so it's a good idea to check which power mode your console is using before the preload starts, even if you don't remember changing it. Sleep mode does use more power, but you can switch back to Shutdown once the download is complete.
If your console has been sitting under the TV for the last few years, now is a good time to give it a cleaning before you start playing. Dust buildup is one of the biggest things to keep an eye on if you want to prevent your PlayStation 5 from overheating , as it traps heat inside the console and can even cause it to shut off while you're playing. This is especially important if you're planning to spend a lot of time in "GTA 6" once it releases, since you'll probably be leaving your console running for hours at a time.
Sony actually suggests using a vacuum cleaner (or a similar cleaning tool) to get the dust out, and it also recommends keeping the PS5 at least 4 inches away from the wall. Its FAQ also says not to set the console on a long-fiber rug or cover it with a cloth. Microsoft's guidance for the Xbox Series X|S asks for 4 to 6 inches of space on all sides and at least 1.5 inches on top, and it says to avoid closed cabinet doors if possible.

articles.title_orig: Nasa seeks next generation of astronauts to live and work on the moon
articles.title_zh: Nasa seeks next generation of astronauts to live and work on the moon
articles.content_orig:
Applications due on 3 December for new generation of explorers who can ‘shape humanity’s future in space’
Nasa has launched a callout for a new generation of astronauts as it searches for explorers who could live and work on the moon.
Opening applications for the latest expansion of its Artemis program , the US agency said successful candidates would help “shape humanity’s future in space” as it builds a base on the moon and plans the first crewed missions to Mars.
The news was announced on Saturday during a Kennedy Space Center air show promoting lunar exploration, as well as advances in aviation and technology.
“This is an extraordinary time to join Nasa’s astronaut corps,” said Nasa administrator Jared Isaacman. “The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars.”
Nasa expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training the next class of astronaut candidates. The agency last opened applications for new astronauts in 2024, ultimately accepting 10 new astronauts out of more than 8,000 applicants in September 2025.
“For those who apply, becoming a Nasa astronaut is more than a career opportunity,” said Scott Tingle, chief astronaut and chair of the Astronaut Selection Board at Nasa’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. “It is a chance to join a legacy of explorers who have pushed the boundaries of discovery and play a role in the missions that will shape humanity’s future in space.”
Since the 1960s, Nasa has selected 370 people to train as astronaut candidates for increasingly challenging missions. The agency currently has 32 astronauts active in the astronaut corps.
Isaacman and other agency leaders recently laid out Nasa’s ambitions to return Americans to the moon in 2028. Both SpaceX and Blue Origin intend to support a crewed lunar landing.
All applicants must be US citizens, Nasa said, and have either a master’s degree in science, technology, engineering or mathematics; medical qualifications; training as a pilot; or two years’ work on a relevant doctoral program.
Three years of “related professional experience” are also required.
Applying pilots must have either 750 hours of pilot-in-command time of a high-performance jet, 1,500 total flight hours in another fixed-wing aircraft, or 1,000 total flight hours in a rotary-wing aircraft.
Applicants have until 11.59pm ET on Thursday, 3 December, to submit their applications.

articles.title_orig: Hacked Records Show 400,000 Russians Killed in War on Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Hacked Records Show 400,000 Russians Killed in War on Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
The hacker groups Kiberpartizany BY and Silent Crow claim to have carried out a large-scale breach of Russia's Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat).
According to the hackers, they managed to steal about 23 terabytes of data, including internal documents, demographic and economic statistics, as well as information on Russian losses in the war against Ukraine.
The data obtained enabled the groups to make their own calculations of the number of people killed since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
According to Kiberpartizany BY, as of 27 August 2026 at least 393,881 Russian citizens have been killed in the war. Silent Crow gives an even higher figure of 450,100 dead.
This significant difference in estimates is due to the use of different methods of counting losses.
Kiberpartizany BY counted deaths in which military action or its consequences were listed as the cause.
Silent Crow, by contrast, not only included those killed in combat, but also added several other categories of deaths: non-combat losses among military personnel, deaths marked as terrorist acts, and deaths of people registered in Russia but who died in occupied territories or in Ukraine where the exact cause of death was not established.
Russia has not released official statistics on combat losses since September 2022.
In addition, from 2024 Rosstat stopped publishing annual data on causes of death, which has made an independent assessment of the demographic impact of the war much more difficult.
Against this backdrop, access to the agency's internal statistical materials may make it possible to assess the scale of human losses more accurately.
For comparison, as of 8 November the joint database of BBC News Russian Service and Mediazona, which collects a list of dead Russian servicemen identified by name, contained around 286,000 names. However, this list is known to be incomplete, especially for the most recent months of the war.
In a joint study by Meduza and Mediazona, based on analysis of inheritance registry data, the number of fallen Russian servicemen by the end of 2025 was estimated at roughly 350,000.
In this way, the hackers' estimates are in line with figures from previously published independent studies, although this does not yet prove the accuracy of each individual number.
Meduza and Mediazona have said they obtained access to the data published by the hackers and have begun checking it.
The journalists aim to establish not only whether the materials are authentic, but also how complete the information is they contain. In particular, they need to rule out the possibility of deliberate data falsification.
Moreover, causes of death given in medical documents do not always reflect the actual circumstances of a person's death.
It should also be noted that Rosstat's internal databases do not contain up-to-date information on people listed as missing. Such individuals may be declared dead only after a long period of time.
Therefore even data from the state statistics agency cannot automatically provide a definitive figure for Russian military losses.
If the authenticity and completeness of the leak are confirmed, the materials obtained could become one of the largest sources of information on the demographic consequences of the war for Russia.

articles.title_orig: I was an international flight attendant. At 36, I'm a part-time receptionist, and I'm happier than ever.
articles.title_zh: I was an international flight attendant. At 36, I'm a part-time receptionist, and I'm happier than ever.
articles.content_orig:
I was born in a small town in Ukraine , raised with the quiet, persistent belief that to succeed, I had to work three times harder than anyone born in a big city. In my early adulthood, my biggest mistake was assuming that only major cities could offer real opportunities — and that I could simply squeeze my mental health into my schedule whenever I happened to have time for it.
Moving to Kyiv in my early 20s felt like the ultimate dream: a chance to prove I belonged. But to survive there, I felt I had to fit a precise, demanding system. It wasn't enough to simply stay healthy; you were expected to hold a premium membership at a high-end fitness center just to prove your worth to others. You had to maintain an active, highly visible social life, eat at the right places, and project total composure. Everything was about trying to impress others.
After I graduated from college , I set my sights on becoming an international flight attendant for Ukraine's national carrier. When I landed the job, I thought I had made it. Instead, impostor syndrome hit me on day one. I felt like I was constantly falling behind my peers, so I ran as fast as I could to outrun the feeling.
I improved my English, started learning Spanish , and took on a summer schedule so punishing I was barely ever home. I spent years living out of a suitcase, navigating time zone changes, early-morning wake-up calls, and strict corporate beauty standards . I measured my worth entirely by my exhaustion, treating a packed calendar as proof that I mattered. Saying "no" to friends because of work became a badge of honor.
Looking back, I knew I was burning out, but I was too overwhelmed to stop. I believed that as long as I was busy, I was safe from failure.
Then, life shifted violently. After having my son, the pandemic grounded the aviation industry. Not long after, war broke out in Ukraine .
We didn't choose to leave our home or plan to emigrate — war made that decision for us, uprooting our family overnight. We ended up settling in a small Ontario town — the exact kind of tranquil environment I had spent my youth trying to escape. When I first arrived, I was terrified. It was so overwhelmingly still and peaceful that, for the first time in my life, I started to hear my own thoughts.
My body, conditioned by a decade of high-tension striving and constant mobility, couldn't handle the sudden stillness. Shortly after arriving, my first panic attack hit me. In the stillness, a painful truth surfaced: I had never once allowed myself to just stay with myself. My mind had always been stuffed with the next goal, the next achievement, or the next deadline. I initially believed that this small town marked the end of my ambition, but as the silence forced me to look inward, I realized I had spent nearly 10 years chasing an illusion.
Unlearning that mindset wasn't immediate; slowing down turned out to be a skill I had to learn from scratch. In the fall of 2022, I found a part-time job as a receptionist in Canada, where I still work today. For the first time in my professional life, I wasn't navigating a massive corporate hierarchy or competing with thousands of employees. Working alongside just three colleagues in a calm atmosphere, I joined a community where people actually knew my name.
Create a BI Job Scout and get opportunities matched to your goals.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
Instead of chasing the next status symbol, I made learning who I actually was my top priority. I no longer pay for an expensive gym membership to impress anyone; instead, I feel fit and strong through my home workouts. Practicing yoga in peace and serenity without a studio full of strangers makes far more sense to me now.
It turns out I love early mornings. I love making my own sauerkraut and keeping a sourdough starter alive to bake rye bread. Baking fresh cinnamon rolls for our neighbors as a small thank-you for their support became one of the most grounding, relaxing rituals of my new life.  I started learning French — not to climb a career ladder or get immigration points, but purely for the joy of the process. There are no deadlines now. I take my time, allow myself to feel stuck, and share my struggles openly with my tutor.
Now, at 36, I build my daily life entirely around my mental health, rather than trying to squeeze my well-being into the leftover cracks of a high-stress career. I refuse to operate in panic mode anymore. Opening my eyes to this required hard choices — letting go of old ambitions, old habits, and even certain relationships. Today, I don't maintain a big circle of friends, but I make intentional time for the special people in my life.
Above all, this inner shift saved more than just my own peace — it transformed my marriage. In my old life, I was always home in body, but absent in spirit; my mind was constantly preoccupied with ambition. As I traded endless chasing for small, quiet moments of joy, my husband and I found a depth of connection we hadn't known was missing. Forced to flee our home because of war, we faced a crisis that could have fractured our relationship. Instead, choosing a simpler, more intentional life together bound us closer and made our family resilient in ways speed never could.
I no longer want to fit in. I prefer to belong — and there is a profound difference between the two. Through simple daily rituals, writing my weekly column, and the gentle warmth of a small community, I finally found the peace I spent a decade trying to chase in the skies.

Season 1 of MW4 is here! The team is currently working on a series of updates that we’ll be releasing over the coming days. Stay tuned for more.

We're not done yet! We have even more #MW4 fixes and improvements rolling out later today with the start of Season 1. These notes are an addition to today's already published notes and have been added separately for easier viewing.
Season 1 brings new content, gameplay updates, and improvements across Modern Warfare 4, with quality of life changes and balance updates coming to Multiplayer and DMZ.
In Multiplayer, four Maps join the rotation, including the return of Shoot House, alongside new Modes, Weapons, and Attachments. Season 1 also introduces a new 100-tier Battle Pass and a series of in-game Events, with additional content planned throughout the Season. We’ve also got fresh weapon tuning for the season.
DMZ expands with the arrival of a new Exclusion Zone, X01. Explore an underground GRANIT Arms facility beneath Hajin. Players can discover new areas, take on additional DMZ Orders, and encounter new threats and equipment as they venture deeper.
More Patch Notes? We’ll be sharing more updates ahead of Season 1’s launch later today. Let’s get after it.
Warzone Agent is an unauthorized, paid third-party application that enables "lobby shopping," allowing players to assess lobby skill levels during pre-match warm-ups and avoid more competitive matches in favor of easier ones. While Warzone Agent does not provide traditional cheating functionality, such as aimbots or wallhacks, it creates an unfair advantage, undermines competitive integrity, and violates our Terms of Use.
Lookout for additional intel soon as additional events (including camo events, DMZ events and more) will arrive throughout Season 1 and Season 1 Reloaded .
Season 1 introduces a streamlined, linear 100-tier Battle Pass. Modern Warfare 4’s Battle Pass launches with a new system that automatically catches players up to the reward corresponding with the current day of the Season, up to Day 50. Battle Pass owners who complete all 100 tiers will also have an opportunity to earn additional bonus rewards later in the Season.
The Season 1 Battle Pass content includes:
Four maps join the rotation with Season 1. Backstab takes the fight to a snow-covered town, while Canyon mixes open spaces with natural terrain and elevation.
Shoot House returns with its familiar three-lane layout in a new setting, and Kill Block: Crash brings a new featured combo for 6v6 gameplay. Expect additional maps later in the season.
Season 1 brings back the Grind mode, where players collect and bank Dog Tags to score, alongside Drop Zone, which puts teams in control of a rotating objective to earn Killstreak drops.
Two additional weapons and several new attachments will join your armory over the course of Season 1.
Season 1 takes DMZ deeper underground with X01, a newly discovered GRANIT Arms black site accessible through Hajin. Expect a new environment to explore, additional Orders, new threats and equipment, FOB updates, and Events throughout the Season.
As always, please share your experiences with us. We plan to continue updating with fixes and quality of life improvements as often as we can.

articles.title_orig: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing four people and injuring dozens more, authorities say
articles.title_zh: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing four people and injuring dozens more, authorities say
articles.content_orig:
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital of Cairo, killing at least seven people and injuring more than 100 others, authorities said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 32 miles south of Cairo, when a train traveling to the southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the Transportation Ministry. One of the trains derailed, it said, but did not specify which.
The Health Ministry said at least four people were killed and 88 others were wounded. The injured were taken to nearby hospitals for treatment, it said.
A train driver was among those killed in the collision, the Health Ministry said.
President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi said in a social media post he is following the aftermath of the train collision "with great concern and extend my deepest condolences to the families of those who lost their lives."
"I have directed state agencies to provide the necessary medical care, promptly investigate the circumstances of the accident and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent," he wrote.
Emergency teams and cranes were dispatched to the scene to clear the wreckage and restore train services to their normal schedule as soon as possible, the Egyptian Railway Authority said.
Last September, a train driver and his assistant were injured after two freight trains collided in the same district.
Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.
